ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Government Strengthens Dairy Infrastructure, Livestock Development and Milk Supply Across India
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government Strengthens Dairy Infrastructure, Livestock Development and Milk Supply Across India प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:49PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening the dairy and livestock sectors through sustained investments in milk processing infrastructure, livestock development, fodder availability and market access, while responding to questions in the Lok Sabha today. Addressing concerns regarding remunerative prices for milk, the Government informed the House that no reports have been received by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying indicating that farmers are unable to secure fair prices due to inadequate milk processing or cold chain facilities. Milk procurement prices continue to be determined by dairy cooperatives and private dairies based on prevailing market conditions. To strengthen dairy infrastructure across the country, the Department is implementing two major schemes: National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) Under the NPDD, Bhind and Datia districts of Madhya Pradesh have been included for strengthening milk procurement infrastructure. The Government has approved: Installation of one 3,000-litre Bulk Milk Cooler in Bhind district. Milk collection infrastructure at 34 Dairy Cooperative Societies (DCSs) in Bhind and 14 DCSs in Datia. The Government also informed that no project proposals have been received from these districts under the AHIDF scheme. To address the rising cost of animal feed and fodder, the Government highlighted the ongoing implementation of the National Livestock Mission (NLM) . Under the Mission: 1.62 lakh tonnes of fodder seeds have been produced. 204 feed and fodder enterprise units have been approved. 100 fodder-centric Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) have been established across 19 States to strengthen local supply chains and reduce input costs for livestock farmers. On the supply of milk in the National Capital, the Government stated that, according to the Study on Demand of Milk and Milk Products in India conducted under the National Dairy Plan Phase-I, Delhi's milk demand was estimated at 111 lakh litres per day (LLPD) in 2019 and is projected to reach 173.5 LLPD by 2030. Delhi's milk demand is currently met through supplies from Mother Dairy , GCMMF (Amul) , Delhi Milk Scheme (DMS) , COMFED , Karnataka Milk Federation (KMF) and private dairies, all operating in compliance with food safety standards prescribed by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). The Government stated that no additional measures are presently required, as the existing supply arrangements adequately meet demand. Responding to another question on a proposed National Livestock Development Framework, the Government clarified that Animal Husbandry is a State subject under the Constitution and that there is no proposal to enact a comprehensive national legislation on livestock development. However, the Government emphasized that it continues to support States and Union Territories through flagship initiatives including the Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) , National Livestock Mission (NLM) , Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) , National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) and the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) . The Government highlighted the sector's strong performance over the past decade: Milk production has increased from 146.31 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 248.87 million tonnes in 2024-25 , representing a 70% increase . Egg production has grown from 78.48 billion to 149.11 billion during the same period, marking a 90% increase . To further enhance exports and livestock traceability, the Department has collaborated with the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) to develop the Bharat Pashudhan database , based on a unique 12-digit Tag ID for livestock. The Government is also promoting investment through AHIDF and NLM while implementing the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme to create disease-free zones and improve export opportunities for Indian livestock products. The Government reiterated its commitment to modernizing dairy infrastructure, improving livestock productivity, strengthening value chains, supporting farmers, ensuring nutritional security and enhancing the global competitiveness of India's dairy and livestock sector. *** SM/ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290496) आगंतुक पटल  : 138 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government Strengthens Dairy Infrastructure, Livestock Development and Milk Supply Across India प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: INLAND FISHERIES INFRASTRUCTURE UNDER PMMSY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying INLAND FISHERIES INFRASTRUCTURE UNDER PMMSY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:09PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total cost of Rs. 20,750 crore with effect from the financial year 2020-21 for the development of fisheries sector in all States/Union Territories including Uttar Pradesh.  The State-wise details of projects approved under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for overall development of fisheries including infrastructure, including ponds, reservoirs, hatcheries, feed mills and cold chain facilities from 2020-21 till date are furnished at Annexure-I. Further, the Department under the PMMSY has accorded approval to the various fisheries developmental proposals of Government of Uttar Pradesh at a total cost of Rs.  1294.32 crore with central liability of Rs. 412.30 crore. Against this central liability,  Rs.336.61 crore has been released for development of Fisheries in the State against which  an expenditure of Rs. 316.61 Crore has been incurred.  As reported by the Government of Uttar Pradesh, PMMSY has been implemented across all districts including the eastern region of the State and assistance is provided for scientific aquaculture, integrated fish farming, pond development, hatcheries, reservoirs, feed mills, cold chain infrastructure, Biofloc, Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS), cage culture and other modern fisheries interventions based on requirements of the State Government. Further, a state-of-art wholesale fish market has been constructed at Chandauli to boost fisheries in eastern region of Uttar Pradesh. Besides, a Pangasius cluster has also been identified in Sidharth Nagar district for the aquaculture development in fast track mode in eastern region of Uttar Pradesh. (d):     The Government is promoting enhanced fish production and income generation of fishers through the various interventions under PMMSY, including aquaculture expansion, infrastructure development, modern technologies, post-harvest management, cold chain facilities, value addition and market linkages. These interventions have contributed significantly to the growth of the fisheries sector in the country, including in Uttar Pradesh. title: Traditional Fisheries
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Traditional Fisheries प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR-CMFRI) has assessed that the trawl-based landings have shown no palpable decline in fish landings during 2021-2025. As per the Marine Fish Stock Status of India (20 2 2) publication of the ICAR-CMFRI, the marine fish stocks of the Indian waters are in good health , and 91.1% of the 135 fish stocks evaluated in different regions of the Indian EEZ were found sustainable. ‘Fisheries’ is a state subject, and each Coastal State has its Marine Fishing Regulation Act (MFRA) for governance of fishing activities within the territorial waters up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline, including zoning of fishing areas for traditional and mechanised fishing vessels, mesh‑size and gear regulations, seasonal fishing bans, minimum legal-size limits for fish capture, prohibition of destructive fishing practices such as paired/bull trawling and use of artificial/LED lights, and prevention of juvenile fishing. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), under which activities such as installation of Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) in trawl nets for protecting the sea turtles, sea ranching, and installation of artificial reefs in coastal waters towards enhancing fish stocks are undertaken for safeguarding the livelihood interests of traditional fishers. PMMSY also promotes acquisition of deep-sea fishing vessels, open-sea cage culture, and mariculture, including seaweed farming to divert fishing pressure away from the inshore coastal waters . The ICAR-CMFRI has informed that it conducts long-term monitoring of marine fisheries and ecosystems using a statistically validated, FAO-recommended stratified multistage random sampling design. The ICAR-CMFRI generates high-quality time-series data on fish landings and fishing effort from over 1,300 landing centres along India's 11,000 km coastline to assess fish stock status and infer ecosystem changes. Further, Institute also informed that it implements national programmes on marine biodiversity, benthic ecosystem health, trophic interactions, and the impacts of bottom trawling. This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying FISH PRODUCTION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India with effect from the Financial Year 2020-21 is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in the country. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India during the last six years has approved fisheries development projects of 34 States/Union Territories and other implementing agencies amounting to Rs.21,461 crore with Central share of Rs.9,571 crore and a sum of Rs.6,206 crore has been released to various States/UTs and other implementing agencies under PMMSY. State-wise details of the projects approved, central share and funds released during the last six years are furnished at Annexure-I. The PMMSY during last five years of its implementation has made vital contribution towards augmentation of fish production, enhancement of fisheries exports and creating of livelihood and employment opportunities. The fish production in the country has increased from 141.64 lakh tonne (2019-20) to an all time record of 197.75 lakh tonne (2024-25), creation of direct and indirect employment opportunities to 58 lakh persons in fisheries and aquaculture related activities, increase of fisheries export from Rs.46,663 crore (2019-20) to Rs.73,890 crore (2025-26). The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog, Government of India has evaluated the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana along with other Centrally Sponsored Schemes and the evaluation study while underlining the impact created by PMMSY in the fisheries sector has recommended its continuation. The PMMSY has been continued till September, 2026 in its existing form. During the current financial year (2026-27), a Central budget of Rs.2500 crore has been allocated for this scheme. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) implemented by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India inter-alia provides financial assistance for setting up of Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) to economically empower the fishers, fish farmers and enhance their bargaining power. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India during the last five years (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26) has approved projects worth of Rs.544.86 crore for formation of 2195 FFPOs in the country with support in the form of incubation cost, management cost and equity grant. This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying TRADITIONAL FISHERMEN AND FISH FARMERS IN TAMIL NADU प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) is implementing various schemes and programs for holistic development of fisheries sector and to enhance the livelihood, income and socio-economic welfare of traditional fishermen and fish farmers in the country including Tamil Nadu, such as Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) (2020-21 to 2024-25), Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (2018-19 to 2025-26), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (2023-24 to 2026-27) and Extension of the facility of the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) to the fishers and fish farmers to meet their working capital requirements. In the state of Tamil Nadu, a project titled "Establishment of Multipurpose Seaweed Park" has been sanctioned under the PMMSY at a total cost of Rs. 127.71 crore, including component of seaweed multiplication in Hub-I Centre at Valamavur in Ramanathapuram District. Under PMMSY and schemes of State Government of Tamil Nadu implemented in Ramanathapuram district in the last three financial years (2023-2026), financial assistance in the form of subsidies, insurance coverage and livelihood support has been provided to traditional fishermen and fish farmers for various activities, as detailed in Annexure I . (c):      The details of fisheries infrastructure developed in Ramanathapuram district, including fishing harbours, fish landing centres, cold storage facilities, ice plants, fish processing units and aquaculture infrastructure are provided at Annexure II . (d):    The Government organizes various skill development and capacity-building programmes for fishermen and fish farmers to enhance their technical skills, disseminate recent innovations and best practices in the fisheries sector, and promote sustainable livelihood opportunities. These training programmes contribute to the livelihood development and socio-economic upliftment of fisher families. 88 training programs covering about 5599 trainees were conducted in the previous 3 years for fishers and fish farmers in Ramanathapuram district. The details are given in Annexure III . (e): The Government is implementing various schemes to promote sustainable fisheries and enhance the livelihood of traditional fishing communities in Ramanathapuram district. Financial assistance and institutional credit is provided for acquisition of 45 deep-sea tuna fishing vessels. In Ramanthapuram District 13,949 Fishermen and farmers are facilitated with access to institutional credit of Rs. 236.26 crore through the Kisan Credit Card (KCC). Further, mariculture activities such as seaweed cultivation and cage culture are being actively promoted to provide alternative livelihood opportunities for fishers and coastal communities. So far, 19,575 seaweed culture rafts and monolines and 499 cage culture units have been established in different districts of Tamil Nadu including Ramanthapuram under various Government schemes. In addition, skill development and capacity-building programmes are regularly organized on seaweed farming, aquaculture and mariculture practices, value addition of fishery products, dry fish processing, preparation of ready-to-eat fish products, boat driving, marine engine repair and maintenance, net crafting, and recycling of waste fishing nets to enhance the technical skills and income-generating capacity of beneficiaries. ***** Annexure-I Statement regarding Traditional Fishermen and Fish Farmers in Tamil Nadu S. title: TRADITIONAL FISHERFOLK IN KERALA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying TRADITIONAL FISHERFOLK IN KERALA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) is implementing various schemes for holistic development of fisheries sector in all States/UTs including Kerala. The major schemes include Blue Revolution Scheme (2015-16 to 2019-20), extending Kisan Credit Card (KCC) to fisheries (since 2018-19), Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) (2018-19 to 2025-26), ‘Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana’ (PMMSY)’ (2020-21 to 2026-27), and a new Central Sector Sub-scheme viz. Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) (2023-24 to 2026-27). Enhancing fish production, ensuring sustainability of resources, strengthening of value chain, employment generation, safety & security of fishers and socio-economic wellbeing of fishers and fish farmers have been the core of these initiatives. During last five years and current financial year (FY 2026-27) under PMMSY, DoF, GoI has accorded approvals to the fisheries development proposal of Government of Kerala amounting to Rs. 1413.91 crore. The approved activities inter-alia include livelihood support to fishers during fishing ban period, support to traditional fishers for procurement of boats and nets, establishment of integrated modern coastal fishing villages, establishment of climate resilient coastal fishing villages, additional and alternate livelihood activities such as bivalve cultivation, cage culture, ornamental fisheries, fish markets & kiosks, cold chain facilities, live fish vending centres, need based training and skill development programmes and development of fishing harbours and marketing facilities etc. The Central Government allocates Superior Kerosene Oil (SKO) on a quarterly basis, but its distribution within a State/UT under the Public Distribution System (PDS) is entirely managed by the respective State/UT Government. The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoP&NG) being the nodal Ministry on the subject matter has informed that as kerosene is a polluting fuel and adversely impacts public health, the PDS Kerosene allocation to States/UTs including Kerala have been rationalized since 2010-11. Till date, 21 States/UTs have become PDS Kerosene free. Government has formulated a new “PDS Kerosene Allocation Policy” for the period of 2025-26 to 2027-28 after stakeholders consultation including the Government of Kerala. As per the said Policy, the allocation is made to States/UTs under single category “PDS SKO” on quarterly basis for cooking & lighting and for special needs. Further, the State Governments have been given the liberty to sub-allocate PDS SKO for cooking and lighting or for special needs (fisheries, mela, exhibitions, pandemic, calamity etc.) based on their specific requirement. Distribution of PDS SKO within State/UT under PDS network is carried out by concerned State/UT. Scale and Criteria of distribution is, accordingly, also decided by respective State/UT. MoPNG has further informed that under the new policy, the Government of Kerala has been allocated 22,704 KL PDS SKO for the year 2025-26 as against total allocation of 4,368 KL PDS SKO for the year 2024-25 which reflects an increase of 419.78 %. During the FY 2025-26 out of the allocated quantity of 22,704 KL the State uplifted 17,724 KL with a lapse of 4,980 KL. It is also informed that, in view of the prevailing geo-political situation an adhoc allocation of 1716 KL PDS SKO was also made for cooking and lighting to the State vide MoPNG’s letter dated 12.03.2026 for upliftment till 30 th June 2026. Out of the allocated quantity, the state uplifted 1512 KL only lapsing 204 KL. Further, an allocation of 4068 KL/quarter has been made to the State of Kerala for Q1 (April-June, 2026) and Q2 (July-September, 2026), 2026-27. This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying BLUE ECONOMY PROJECTS IN ANDHRA PRADESH प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) has been implementing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY):  A scheme to bring about Blue Revolution through sustainable and responsible development of fisheries sector in India’ in all States and Union Territories (UTs) including the State of Andhra Pradesh, since 2020-21. Under PMMSY, for the development of fisheries and fisheries infrastructure in the State, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has approved proposals of the Government of Andhra Pradesh at a total cost of Rs 2328.89 crore, with a central share of Rs 681.38 crore. An amount of Rs 445.05 Crore has been released to the State based on the State's utilization. The year-wise details of projects approved, fund sanctioned and released during the last six years under PMMSY for furnished at Annexure I . The major fisheries infrastructure projects approved under PMMSY for development of fisheries in the State of Andhra Pradesh include (i) establishment of 5 fish feed plants, (ii) 16 cold storages and ice plants, (iii) 6 modern fish landing centres, (iv) 3 modern fishing harbours, (v) modernization of fishing harbour at Vishakhapatnam and (vi) 1 integrated Aqua Park. In addition, 15 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV) and one Fish Brood Bank have also been sanctioned. The Government is closely monitoring developments in the global trade environment, including geopolitical situations, through regular engagement with stakeholders and export promotion agencies. While no separate State-specific assessment has been carried out on the impact of the West Asia conflict on seafood exports from Andhra Pradesh, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has undertaken several initiatives to address emerging trade challenges. These initiatives include a Seafood Exporters Meet in April 2026, New Delhi and National Workshop on Seafood Exports at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh in June 2026, wherein issues relating to market diversification, Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), non-tariff barriers, traceability, logistics and export competitiveness were deliberated with stakeholders. Despite the prevailing global geopolitical and trade challenges, various efforts taken by the Government of India has resulted in India's seafood exports recording an all-time high of 19.72 lakh metric tonnes valued at ₹73,890.46 crore (US$ 8.46 billion) during the financial year 2025–26. *** Annexure I Statement regarding Blue Economy Projects in Andhra Pradesh (Rupees in Lakhs) Sl. The major fisheries infrastructure projects approved under PMMSY for development of fisheries in the State of Andhra Pradesh include (i) establishment of 5 fish feed plants, (ii) 16 cold storages and ice plants, (iii) 6 modern fish landing centres, (iv) 3 modern fishing harbours, (v) modernization of fishing harbour at Vishakhapatnam and (vi) 1 integrated Aqua Park. In addition, 15 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV) and one Fish Brood Bank have also been sanctioned. The Government is closely monitoring developments in the global trade environment, including geopolitical situations, through regular engagement with stakeholders and export promotion agencies. While no separate State-specific assessment has been carried out on the impact of the West Asia conflict on seafood exports from Andhra Pradesh, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has undertaken several initiatives to address emerging trade challenges. These initiatives include a Seafood Exporters Meet in April 2026, New Delhi and National Workshop on Seafood Exports at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh in June 2026, wherein issues relating to market diversification, Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), non-tariff barriers, traceability, logistics and export competitiveness were deliberated with stakeholders. Despite the prevailing global geopolitical and trade challenges, various efforts taken by the Government of India has resulted in India's seafood exports recording an all-time high of 19.72 lakh metric tonnes valued at ₹73,890.46 crore (US$ 8.46 billion) during the financial year 2025–26. *** Annexure I Statement regarding Blue Economy Projects in Andhra Pradesh (Rupees in Lakhs) Sl. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying DEVELOPMENT OF RESERVOIRS AND AMRIT SAROVARS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi (a): The Government of India in the Union Budget, 2026-27 has announced the development of fisheries and aquaculture by undertaking integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in the country including Bastar  constituency in Chhattisgarh. The initiative reinforces the Government’s objective to harvest the untapped fisheries potential from reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, strengthening livelihoods of fishermen in the reservoirs and engagement of women self-help groups (SHGs), fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPO) for the development of fisheries in Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. The key components of this initiative  includes strengthening quality seed production by establishing hatchery, promotion of cage and pen culture in reservoir, providing boats and nets to reservoir fishermen, promotion of composite fish culture and integrated fish farming in the Amrit Sarovar, establishment of fisheries infrastructure such as fish feed mill, cold storage, ice plant, fish kiosk and retail fish market, fish transport vehicle and fish value addition units. (b) to (d): The selection of the Reservoirs and Amrit sarovars  by the  Department of Fisheries (DoF), Government of India (GoI) has been done in consultation with States and Union Territories (UTs), considering the perennial water availability and fisheries potential of the identified reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. Accordingly, 12 number of reservoirs and 5 numbers of Amrit Sarovars from Bihar and 27 reservoirs and 5 Amrit Sarovars from Chhattisgarh including Kosardeda reservoir from Bastar Constituency has been selected. District-wise reservoir selected in Chhattisgarh in consultation with the State Government is at Annexure-III. (e) The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) with the objective of enhancing fishers’ income in the country is promoting involvement of Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups and fisheries cooperatives under the Integrated development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. This includes the formation of Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups, and fisheries cooperatives, as well as support for existing ones, in the selected reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. (f) The investment for the implementation of the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars is to be based on the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the States and Union Territories (UTs). title: GAIS FOR FISHERMEN
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying GAIS FOR FISHERMEN प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:55PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total investment of Rs. 20,750/- crore from the financial year 2020-21 to till date for development of fisheries in all States/Union Territories.  The scheme inter-alia provides social security measure to fishers, fish workers through group accidental insurance coverage to both marine and inland fishers and allied fish workers wherein the entire insurance premium amount is shared between the Centre  and State in the ratio of 60:40, 90:10 for the Himalayan & North Eastern States and in the case of the Union Territories, the entire premium amount is paid by the Centre. The insurance coverage provided under the PMMSY includes (i) Rs.5,00,000/- against death or permanent total disability, (ii) Rs.2,50,000/- for permanent partial disability and (iii) hospitalization expenses in the event of accident for a sum of Rs. 25,000/. The year wise and State/UT wise details of claims filed, claims approved, claims rejected, claims pending, and total compensation disbursed under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) for fishermen since 2020 21 are furnished at Annexure-I. (b)       During the last five years (2021-22 to 2025-26) and current finance year (2026-27) of the implementation of the PMMSY, an average of 35.74 lakh active fishers have been enrolled under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS), annually. The average State/UT-wise details of fishers enrolled and coverage percentage of the total estimated fishermen population under Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) are furnished at Annexure-II. (c):       Besides, under the erstwhile Blue Revolution scheme, insurance coverage for fishers was modest, with relatively lower benefit amounts. Based on the suggestions received from State Governments and evaluation of Blue Revolution Scheme, the GAIS coverage under PMMSY has been significantly enhanced both in scale and value to provide increased financial security and risk mitigation to fishers. As such, the sum assured has been increased from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh for accidental death or permanent total disability, ₹1 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh for permanent partial disability, along with ₹10,000/- to Rs. 25,000 hospitalization support, compared to much lower limits under the erstwhile Blue Revolution scheme. ***** Annexure-I Statement regarding GAIS for Fishermen The year wise and State/UT wise details of claims filed, claims approved, claims rejected, claims pending, and total compensation disbursed under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) for fishermen from 2021-22 to 2025-26 Financial Year -2021-2022 COVERAGE PERIOD (From 26.07.2021 to 25.07.2022) SL NO NAME CLAIMS FILED CLAIMS APPROVED CLAIMS REJECTED CLAIMS PENDING TOTAL COMPENSATION DISBURSED (in Rs.) title: ALLOCATION OF FUNDS FOR TAMIL NADU UNDER PMMSY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying ALLOCATION OF FUNDS FOR TAMIL NADU UNDER PMMSY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi (a): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) accorded administrative approvals for the implementation of projects under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) in Tamil Nadu during the period 2020-21 to 2025-26 with a total approved outlay of Rs.1,240.5778 crore. This comprised a Central share of Rs.480.0906 crore, State share of Rs.455.6139 crore, and beneficiary contribution of Rs.272.8488 crore covering both Beneficiary and Non-Beneficiary components. The approved project outlay represents the total financial allocation for the entire scheme period, whereas the Central share is released in phases by the DoF, GoI based on the progress of implementation, submission of Utilisation Certificates (UCs), and compliance with scheme guidelines, etc. Accordingly, the Central assistance is released from time to time, and it does not represent a deficit in the approved project outlay. (b): The details of central funds released under PMMSY to Tamil Nadu, year wise during the last three years (2023-24 to 2025-26) and the details of central funds released under PMMSY in Tirunelveli District of Tamil Nadu are provided at Annexure . The subsidy amounts are directly transferred to the beneficiaries bank accounts through Electronic Clearing Service (ECS). (c): To promote Deep Sea fishing in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), the DoF, GoI had introduced a sub-component namely “Assistance for Deep Sea Fishing” and another component of “Conversion of Trawlers into Resource Specific Deep-Sea Fishing Vessels” under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) on Blue Revolution implemented from 2015-2020. These sub-components were introduced to provide financial assistance to traditional fishermen for promotion of deep-sea fishing in the coastal States/UTs including Tamil Nadu. The financial assistance to traditional fishermen for acquisition of Deep Sea Fishing Vessels (DSFVs) has also been continued under the PMMSY at the rate of 40% subsidy for General Category and 60% subsidy for SC/ST/Women beneficiaries. Support for DSFVs is also provided by the DoF, GoI, under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF). Under PMMSY, financial support is provided to traditional fishers for acquisition of deep-sea fishing vessels (DSFVs) as well as for Upgradation of Existing Fishing Vessels for Export Competency. Under the schemes of Blue Revolution, PMMSY, and the FIDF, projects amounting to Rs.1,314.81 crore have been sanctioned for the acquisition of 1,205 deep-sea fishing vessels by traditional fishers including the fishers of the Tamil Nadu State. The development and modernisation of infrastructure has been accorded high priority under the schemes implemented by the DoF, GoI. Infrastructure projects worth Rs 187.9 crores were sanctioned under Blue Revolution Scheme in Tamil Nadu, which includes fishing harbour project at Mookaiyur and fish landing centre at Kunthukal. Projects worth Rs 155.57 crores have been sanctioned under the PMMSY in Tamil Nadu, which includes three fishing harbour projects viz. modernization of Chennai fishing harbour, upgradation of Pazhayar fishing harbour, maintenance dredging of Colachel fishing harbour; and four fish landing centre projects viz. Nettukupam fish landing centre, Thazankuppam fish landing centre, Arangankuppam fish landing centre, and Goonankuppam fish landing centre. Under Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) scheme, 16 Nos of Fishing Harbours and 57 Fish landing centre have been sanctioned in Tamil Nadu at total project cost of Rs.1988.35 crore. (d): The subsidy/concession rate on fuel to the fishermen has been provided by the respective State Governments/Union Territories, by exercising their powers to frame their own taxation and welfare policies for the fisheries sector. It is informed by the State Government of Tamil Nadu that the Government is providing sales tax exempted diesel to the fishermen for reducing the operational cost of their fishing boats (Both mechanized fishing boats and motorized country crafts) and also providing subsidized industrial kerosene to the motorized country crafts operated in the districts of Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari districts. Under these scheme, Government of Tamil Nadu is providing sales tax exempted diesel of  19,000 L / year / craft to 4,500 Mechanised fishing boats, sales tax exempted diesel of  4,400 L / year / craft to 13,500 Motorized country crafts and subsidized industrial kerosene of 3,700 L / year / craft to around 7500 Motorized country crafts. This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. title: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) Post Highest-Ever Net Profit of Rs. 10,177 Crore in FY 2025–26, show consistent improvement in other key financial parameters
content:

                28 JUL 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India regularly reviews the performance and financial health of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) at national and regional levels. The following reviews of RRBs have been held under the Chairpersonship of Finance Minister in last four financial years: S.No National/Regional level Date and Place 1. National level 07.07.2022 at New Delhi 2. North-Eastern RRBs 21.07.2023 at Agartala 3. Southern RRBs 04.08.2023 at Chennai 4. Northern RRBs 30.08.2023 at New Delhi 5. National level 19.08.2024 at New Delhi 6. Western-Central RRBs 22.08.2024 at Udaipur 7. North-Eastern RRBs 30.09.2024 at Itanagar 8. Southern RRBs 09.11.2024 at Bengaluru 9. Eastern RRBs 29.11.2024 at Patna 10. Karnataka Grameena Bank 16.10.2025 at Ballari Further, as a follow-up, Department of Financial Services (DFS) conducts periodic and regular meetings with RRBs and sponsor banks at various levels. The agenda items for the review meetings, inter-alia , include: Review of the performance of RRBs on financial parameters. Focus on technology upgradation. Thrust on Micro Small and Medium Enterprise (MSME) portfolio. Importance on loan diversification towards Agri-allied, MSME and Retail Sectors. title: Gross Non-Performing Assets (GNPA) of Public Sector Banks (PSBs) at historic low of 1.9% in FY 2025–26, achieve highest-ever net profit of ₹ 1.98 lakh crore; aggregate business reaches over ₹283 lakh crore
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Finance Gross Non-Performing Assets (GNPA) of Public Sector Banks (PSBs) at historic low of 1.9% in FY 2025–26, achieve highest-ever net profit of ₹ 1.98 lakh crore; aggregate business reaches over ₹283 lakh crore Credit Growth Accelerates Across Key Sectors in FY 2025-26; MSME and Retail Loans Register Robust Growth of 19.6% and 19.8% respectively प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:27PM by PIB Delhi The financial health of Public Sector Banks (PSBs) have shown significant improvement with healthy balance sheets, historically high profits and multi-decadal low level of gross non-performing assets (GNPAs). ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Update on Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojna (AB PM-JAY)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojna (AB PM-JAY) AB PM-JAY Achieves Pan-India Implementation; Now Operational Across All 36 States/UTs AB PM-JAY Facilitates Nationwide Healthcare Access Through Portability; 29.05 Lakh Inter-State Admissions Worth ₹8,383.97 Crore Authorized Health Assurance Extended to 6 Crore Senior Citizens Aged 70 Years and Above Health Coverage Network Strengthened; Beneficiary Base Rises from 10.74 Crore to 12 Crore Families Seamless Inter-State Portability Under AB PM-JAY Facilitated by Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitras Through Beneficiary Verification, Cashless Admissions and Hospital Support प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:14PM by PIB Delhi Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) continues to strengthen India’s journey towards Universal Health Coverage by ensuring access to quality, affordable and cashless healthcare services. The scheme is now being implemented across all 36 States/Union Territories, marking a significant milestone in expanding healthcare access and strengthening the delivery of secondary and tertiary care services across the country. Initially, the scheme covered 10.74 crore families identified under the Socio-Economic Caste Census, 2011, constituting the bottom 40% of India’s population. In January 2023, the beneficiary base was revised from 10.74 crore to 12 crore families to account for India's decadal population growth. In March 2024, approximately 37 lakh additional families of Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi Workers and Anganwadi Helpers were included under the scheme. The scheme was further expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status. Further, many States have expanded the beneficiary base beyond the centrally targeted beneficiary numbers by converging their state-specific schemes with AB PM-JAY. The expansion of the beneficiary base under AB PM-JAY, coupled with the integration of various State health assurance schemes, has significantly enhanced the scheme's outreach among vulnerable populations across the country. AB PM-JAY provides a national portability feature, enabling beneficiaries to avail cashless treatment at any empanelled hospital across the country, irrespective of their State/UT. This portability feature enhances access to quality healthcare services, particularly for migrant workers and beneficiaries travelling outside their home State. As on 30 th June, 2026, a total of 29.05 lakh inter-state portability hospital admissions, amounting to more than Rs. 8,383.97 crore, have been authorized under AB PM-JAY across the country. AB PM-JAY is implemented through a robust end-to-end digital platform that enables empanelled hospitals to identify and verify eligible beneficiaries, irrespective of their home State, and facilitates hospital admissions, claims processing and settlement for portability cases. This integrated digital ecosystem ensures seamless, cashless and paperless access to healthcare services at empanelled hospitals across the country. To improve beneficiary enrolment and enhance awareness, including on the portability feature, AB PM-JAY has adopted a comprehensive Information, Education & Communication (IEC) and outreach strategy. The strategy includes awareness campaigns through traditional and digital media platforms such as newspapers, community radio, television and radio campaigns, digital displays, street plays, mass messaging, social media, and the dissemination of beneficiary testimonials. Further, Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitras deployed at empanelled hospitals play a key role in facilitating portability under AB PM-JAY. They assist beneficiaries, including migrant workers and those seeking treatment outside their home State, with identification and verification, cashless admission, hospital coordination, and support throughout the hospitalization process. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Prataprao Jadhav, stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** SR HFW/Update on AB PM-JAY/28July2026/5 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290627) आगंतुक पटल  : 128 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojna (AB PM-JAY) AB PM-JAY Achieves Pan-India Implementation; Now Operational Across All 36 States/UTs AB PM-JAY Facilitates Nationwide Healthcare Access Through Portability; 29.05 Lakh Inter-State Admissions Worth ₹8,383.97 Crore Authorized Health Assurance Extended to 6 Crore Senior Citizens Aged 70 Years and Above Health Coverage Network Strengthened; Beneficiary Base Rises from 10.74 Crore to 12 Crore Families Seamless Inter-State Portability Under AB PM-JAY Facilitated by Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitras Through Beneficiary Verification, Cashless Admissions and Hospital Support प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Measures Taken to Prevent and Control Spread of Monsoon-Related Diseases
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measures Taken to Prevent and Control Spread of Monsoon-Related Diseases 887 Sentinel Surveillance Hospitals, 27 Apex Referral Laboratories and Real-time IHIP Monitoring Strengthen Disease Surveillance Nationwide Supply of Drugs, Diagnostics and Technical Guidelines Enhances Early Detection, Treatment and Outbreak Response Integrated Vector Management Through Indoor Residual Spraying, Bed Nets, Anti-larval Measures and Source Reduction Capacity Building, IEC/BCC Campaigns and Multi-sectoral Convergence Drive Community-based Prevention Across the Country Focused Interventions for Dengue, Malaria, Diarrhoea and Leptospirosis Supported by PPCL, STOP Diarrhoea Campaign and Flood Preparedness Measures प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi The Government has undertaken several measures to prevent and control the spread of monsoon-related diseases in the Country that include: For early diagnosis and complete treatment of malaria, drugs and diagnostics are supplied to the States/UTs through the National Health Mission. For surveillance and free diagnosis of Dengue, a network of 887 Sentinel Surveillance Hospitals (SSHs) and 27 Apex Referral Laboratories (ARLs) identified across the country. GoI provides IgM test kits to all identified laboratories through the National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune. A network of 5 diagnostic labs has been strengthened under the PPCL programme by providing Grant-in-Aid (GIA) for procurement of Equipment’s and consumables. Capacity building and training of trainers, community leaders, and frontline workers to enhance outreach at the grassroots level. Integrated Vector Management including Indoor Residual Spray in selected high-risk areas, Bed Nets in high malaria endemic areas, use of larvivorous fish, anti-larval measures in urban areas, including bio-larvicides and minor environmental engineering and source reduction for prevention of breeding. STOP Diarrhoea Campaign” is conducted which aims at reducing illness and preventing deaths due to Diarrhoea among children under five years of age. The campaign follows the Protect, Prevent and Treat (PPT) strategy and promotes early management of Diarrhoea through Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) and Zinc supplementation. Disease Management involving early case detection with active, passive and sentinel surveillance followed by complete and effective treatment, strengthening of referral services, epidemic preparedness and rapid response. Supportive Interventions aiming at Information Education and Communication (IEC) & Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) and dissemination of public health messages through various media platforms including social media, radio, newspapers, and electronic media. States are trained to enter the data on Integrated Health Information Portal-Vector Borne Diseases (IHIP-VBD) portal for real-time monitoring, Provided Technical Guidelines for case management, prevention and control to the States for implementation. Inter-Sectoral Convergence including high-level advocacy with allied Ministries, Human Resource Development through capacity building and policy development. The Government is actively collaborating with State Health Departments and Urban Local Bodies to enhance sanitation, strengthen mosquito control measures, and increase public awareness for the prevention and control of malaria and other vector-borne diseases (VBDs). Inter-departmental coordination, involving Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Public Distribution System (PDS) members, and religious/community leaders to mobilize communities and promote preventive practices. Advisories are regularly issued to States and Union Territories including to continue promotive, preventive, and curative measures, including outbreak containment. The advisory on leptospirosis emphasizes strengthening case-based surveillance through IDSP, timely reporting, and dissemination of clinical management guidelines with early antibiotic use and ensuring lab preparedness with diagnostic kits like IgM ELISA. National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) is implementing Programme for Prevention and Control of Leptospirosis (PPCL) with aim to reduce morbidity and mortality by strengthening surveillance and diagnostic capacity, raising awareness on early detection and treatment, improving patient management facilities, capacity building and enhancing inter-sectoral coordination for effective outbreak prevention and control. Management of urban flooding falls under the purview of the State Governments and the Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ Urban Development Authorities. The Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India provides financial and technical support to the States for strengthening Urban Planning ecosystem. It supplements the efforts of the States through schematic interventions and issuing various documents/advisory guidelines for improving urban drainage and flood management. Time-to-time advisories/guidance are issued to States/UTs by MoHFW, Government of India for actions to be taken for prevention and control of VBDs and other monsoon-prone diseases in flood-affected areas ensuring rapid deployment of response teams, maintain adequate stocks of diagnostic kits, drugs, insecticides and strengthen disease surveillance systems, close monitoring of situation for early detection and containment of outbreaks. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel, stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. **** SR HFW/Measures Taken to Prevent and Control Spread of Monsoon Related Diseases /28July2026/3 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290626) आगंतुक पटल  : 78 Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measures Taken to Prevent and Control Spread of Monsoon-Related Diseases 887 Sentinel Surveillance Hospitals, 27 Apex Referral Laboratories and Real-time IHIP Monitoring Strengthen Disease Surveillance Nationwide Supply of Drugs, Diagnostics and Technical Guidelines Enhances Early Detection, Treatment and Outbreak Response Integrated Vector Management Through Indoor Residual Spraying, Bed Nets, Anti-larval Measures and Source Reduction Capacity Building, IEC/BCC Campaigns and Multi-sectoral Convergence Drive Community-based Prevention Across the Country Focused Interventions for Dengue, Malaria, Diarrhoea and Leptospirosis Supported by PPCL, STOP Diarrhoea Campaign and Flood Preparedness Measures प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Steps taken to strengthen financial assistance for critical diseases
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps taken to strengthen financial assistance for critical diseases Cashless treatment available for 1,961 procedures under Health Benefit Package-2022 AB PM-JAY expanded to cover 12 crore families; senior citizens and frontline workers also included One‑time aid up to Rs. 15 Lakh via Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi; Health Minister’s Discretionary Grant (HMDG) offers up to Rs. 1.25 Lakh for poor patients Health Benefit Package-2022 enables cashless treatment across 27 specialties, including major non-communicable diseases Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) applications processed online through National Health Authority portal; offline submission also available प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi The Government has implemented several measures to strengthen financial assistance for the treatment of critical diseases by expanding the coverage of health schemes and enhancing access to cashless treatment and financial support. Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) was launched in September 2018 to provide health coverage of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization. Initially, the scheme covered 10.74 crore poor and vulnerable families identified on the basis of deprivation and occupational criteria under the Socio-Economic Caste Census, 2011, in rural and urban areas. In January 2023, the beneficiary base was revised from 10.74 crore to 12 crore families to account for India's decadal population growth. To further strengthen beneficiary identification and expand coverage, alternative beneficiary databases, including the National Food Security Act database and other State-specific beneficiary databases having similar socio-economic criteria were adopted under the scheme. In March 2024, approximately 37 lakh additional families of Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi Workers and Anganwadi Helpers were included under the scheme. The scheme was further expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status. Under the National Master of Health Benefit Package (HBP-2022), cashless treatment is available for 1,961 procedures across 27 medical specialties, covering a wide range of secondary and tertiary care services, including treatment for major non-communicable diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular diseases, chronic kidney disease, diabetes-related complications, stroke, chronic respiratory diseases, neurological disorders, liver diseases etc. Government of India provides one‑time financial assistance up to Rs. 15 lakh under the Umbrella Scheme of Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) for the treatment of poor patients suffering from life‑threatening diseases related to the heart, kidney, liver, and cancer, etc., in Government hospitals/institutes with super‑speciality facilities, subject to fulfilment of the eligibility conditions prescribed under the scheme guidelines. Further, under the Health Minister’s Discretionary Grant (HMDG), financial assistance up to Rs. 1.25 lakh is provided to poor patients suffering from life‑threatening diseases to cover part of the expenditure on hospitalization/treatment in Government hospitals, in cases where free medical facilities are not available, subject to fulfilment of the eligibility conditions prescribed under the scheme guidelines. To apply for assistance under the RAN Scheme, the Nodal Officer of RAN at the concerned Government hospital/institute is to be contacted, who facilitates processing of the case online through the National Health Authority IT portal. However, in case the hospital is not onboarded for online processing of cases under RAN, or encounters technical issues while processing the case online, the patient’s duly filled application in the prescribed format (available with the guidelines of RAN) is required to be forwarded through the treating hospital to the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare for consideration. Further details regarding RAN/HMDG schemes can be accessed at: https://www.mohfw-dohfw.gov.in/ → Offerings → Programmes → Poor Patients Financial Support. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. **** SR HFW/Steps taken to provide financial assistance for critical diseases/28July2026/1 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290623) आगंतुक पटल  : 69 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps taken to strengthen financial assistance for critical diseases Cashless treatment available for 1,961 procedures under Health Benefit Package-2022 AB PM-JAY expanded to cover 12 crore families; senior citizens and frontline workers also included One‑time aid up to Rs. 15 Lakh via Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi; Health Minister’s Discretionary Grant (HMDG) offers up to Rs. 1.25 Lakh for poor patients Health Benefit Package-2022 enables cashless treatment across 27 specialties, including major non-communicable diseases Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) applications processed online through National Health Authority portal; offline submission also available प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps taken for Licensing Compliance and Formalisation of Small Food Vendors Over 74.33 Lakh Active Food Business Licences and Registrations Issued Under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 FSSAI Simplifies Licensing Framework Through Perpetual Validity, Free Registration for Street Vendors and Tatkal Licensing Government Promotes Formalisation of Food Businesses Through Deemed Registration and Simplified Licensing Reforms Over 2.23 Lakh Food Samples Analysed; More Than 40,000 Non-conforming Samples Detected in 2025–26 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has undertaken several measures to strengthen food safety, simplify regulatory compliance and promote the formalisation of food businesses. FSSAI is mandated to lay down science-based standards for articles of food and regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import to ensure the availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption. The implementation and enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006 is a shared responsibility of the Central and State Governments. To facilitate and encourage informal, small and petty Food Business Operators (FBOs) to come under the formal food safety and licensing framework, FSSAI has implemented the following key measures: Introducing the provision for deemed registration of street food vendors, hawkers, food trucks, carts and similar food businesses registered under the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 to address the dual compliance requirements for street food vendors, registered with municipal corporation and town vending committee. Street food vendors and hawkers are completely exempt from the FSSAI registration fee. Applicable for both new registrations and renewals, eligible vendors can obtain a 5-year registration certificate completely free of charge. To reduce the regulatory burden on FBOs and promote ease of doing business, FSSAI has introduced perpetual validity for licences and registrations. Earlier, licences and registrations were required to be renewed periodically, with validity ranging from one to five years. Under the revised framework, licences and registrations will remain valid indefinitely, thereby eliminating the need for periodic renewals while ensuring continued compliance with the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006, and the rules and regulations made thereunder . Tatkal issuance of License/Registration has been implemented w.e.f. 28 th June 2024 under certain kind of low-risk food businesses such as Wholesalers, Distributors, Retailers, Transporters, Storage without atmospheric control, Importers, Food vending agencies, Direct sellers and Merchant–Exporters. The State-wise details of active Licences and Registrations issued under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 are annexed at Annexure-I. Details of enforcement action taken for all non-conforming foods products (including adulteration) across the country (State-wise) in the last 5 years is annexed at Annexure-II, III, IV, V and VI respectively. ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Union Health Ministry observes World Hepatitis Day 2026; marks eight years of National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Union Health Ministry observes World Hepatitis Day 2026; marks eight years of National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP) Union MoS for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel calls for a Hepatitis-Mukt Bharat; urges collective action by Government, States and stakeholders to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030 India among the few countries providing free-of-cost treatment for Hepatitis C and management of Hepatitis B; access and affordability of services strengthened: Smt. Patel “Hepatitis B birth-dose coverage crosses 92%; States should ensure 100% Hepatitis B screening of pregnant women and strengthen awareness on Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C” Over 21 crore beneficiaries screened, over 6 lakh patients treated, 1,153 treatment centres established and 7.64 crore pregnant women screened under NVHCP: Union Health Secretary NVHCP leverages convergence with the Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) Programme and the National AIDS Control Programme IEC materials on viral hepatitis, modes of transmission and services available under NVHCP released at the event प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:35PM by PIB Delhi Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare today observed World Hepatitis Day 2026 under the global theme “Hepatitis: Let’s Break It Down”, marking eight years of the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP). Launched on World Hepatitis Day in 2018 under the National Health Mission, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the programme reflects India’s commitment to eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030, in line with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 3.3. Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare & Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel, delivered the keynote address, and reaffirmed the Government of India’s commitment to a Hepatitis-Mukt Bharat , and called for intensified efforts by the Government, States and all stakeholders to achieve the goal. Delivering the keynote address, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated that “India is marking eight years of the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme, during which substantial progress has been made in prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.” She noted that “India is among the few countries providing free-of-cost treatment for Hepatitis C and management of Hepatitis B, while continuing to improve access and affordability of services.” She further highlighted that “the cost of medicines has been reduced to less than one dollar, while quality diagnostics are being made increasingly accessible to facilitate early identification and timely treatment.” The Minister said that the programme has been expanded in a phased manner. Initially, treatment services for uncomplicated cases were strengthened at district health facilities, while selected institutions were strengthened to provide referral services for complicated cases. Thereafter, screening and treatment services were expanded to the country's network of more than 1.85 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, thereby expanding access to hepatitis services at the primary healthcare level. Highlighting preventive interventions, Smt. Patel noted that “the Hepatitis B vaccine, introduced under the Universal Immunization Programme in 2011, has achieved more than 92 percent birth-dose coverage.” She emphasised that “while around 65 percent of pregnant women are currently being screened for Hepatitis B, States and Union Territories should work towards 100 percent screening to ensure timely administration of the Hepatitis B birth dose for all eligible newborns and Hepatitis B Immunoglobulin (HBIG) within 24 hours for newborns of Hepatitis B-positive mothers.” The Minister also stressed the importance of vaccinating healthcare workers to prevent occupational transmission and called for focused interventions among high-risk populations to protect vulnerable groups from chronic liver disease and liver cancer. Describing Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C as “silent killers”, she underlined the need to generate greater public awareness and urged States and Union Territories to educate communities that testing and treatment services are available at government health facilities. Reaffirming that “health is a shared goal”, Smt. Patel said that “the Government of India, State Governments and all stakeholders must continue working together with renewed commitment to achieve the goal of eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030.” Expressing confidence in the country’s collective efforts, she stated that “sustained and intensified efforts would help realise the vision of a Hepatitis-Mukt Bharat .” On the occasion, Smt. Patel also released Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials, including posters on Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C, highlighting modes of transmission and services available under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP) for dissemination across States and Union Territories. Addressing the gathering, Union Health Secretary, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, highlighted the significant progress achieved under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme. title: PM E-DRIVE SCHEME AND PROMOTION OF ELECTRIC MOBILITY
content:

                28 JUL 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi (a) the salient features, objectives, financial outlay and present status of the PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) Scheme, including the categories of electric vehicles covered and the incentives provided thereunder; (b) the details of incentives released and the number of beneficiaries, EV supported, charging stations sanctioned and e-buses deployed under the scheme since its launch, State-wise; (c) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the impact of the scheme on accelerating electric vehicle adoption, reducing fossil fuel consumption, lowering vehiculare missions and promoting domestic manufacturing under the 'Make in India' initiative and if so, the details thereof; (d) the details of measures taken to strengthen charging infrastructure, battery manufacturing and recycling ecosystems under the scheme; and (e) whether the Government proposes to extend special incentives for Tier-II and Tier-III cities and aspirational regions to promote wider adoption of electric mobility and support the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047? ANSWER THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) (a) & (b): The salient features, objectives, financial outlay and present status of PM E-DRIVE Scheme including categories of electric vehicles covered and the incentive provided thereunder are as under: i.                The primary objective of the PM E-DRIVE scheme is for faster adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), setting up of charging infrastructure and development of EV manufacturing eco-system in the country. ii.              The total outlay of the scheme is ₹10,900 crore. iii.             The categories of EVs covered and applicable incentive rate is as provided in table below: Category FY 2024-25 FY 2025-26 to FY 2027-28 e-2W ₹5,000 / kWh, capped at ₹10,000 per vehicle* ₹2,500 / kWh, capped at ₹5,000 per vehicle (up to 31.07.2026)* e-3W (registered e-rickshaws & e-carts) ₹5,000 / kWh, capped at ₹25,000 per vehicle* ₹2,500 / kWh, capped at ₹12,500 per vehicle* e-3W (L5) ₹5,000 / kWh, capped at  ₹50,000 per vehicle (up to 07.11.2024)* ₹2,500 / kWh, capped at ₹25,000 per vehicle (08.11.2024 to 26.12.2025)* -2- Category FY 2024-25 FY 2025-26 to FY 2027-28 * The incentive for e-2W/ e-3W is further capped at 15% of ex-factory price. e-truck - ₹5,000 / kWh, capped at 10% of ex-factory price (excl. trailer)# # The incentive for e-truck is further capped based on the GVW of the e-truck as per table below : GVW (ton) >3.5 & <=7.5 >7.5 & <=12 >12 & <=18.5 >18.5 & <=35 >35 & <=55 Max. incentive per e-truck (₹ lakh) 2.7 3.6 7.8 9.6 9.3 e-ambulance - ₹30,000 / kWh, capped at 35% of ex-factory price e-bus ₹10,000 / kWh, capped at 20% of cost of vehicle (as per prices discovered by CESL) and further capped based on length of e-bus as below: ₹35,00,000 per e-bus for length > 10metre(m) <= 12m; ₹25,00,000 per e-bus for length > 8m & <= 10m; ₹20,00,000 per e-bus for length > 6m & <= 8m. iv.  Present Status: The scheme was notified on September 29, 2024 and implemented w.e.f. 01.04.2024 since EMPS 2024 has been subsumed to PM E-DRIVE Scheme and is currently being implemented upto March 31, 2028 (terminal dates for e-2W segment is 31.07.2026 and scheme for e-3W (L5) was closed on 26.12.2025. The details of EVs incentivised under the scheme are as under : (As on 22.07.2026) Category No. of EVs Incentivized Incentive Amount Reimbursed to OEMs (Rs. Crore) e-2w 20,56,831 1,505.30 e-3w: e-rickshaw/ e-cart 5,082 7.61 e-3w: L5 2,60,965 769.02 Total 23,22,878 2,281.94 Further no state-wise allocation has been done for the demand incentive category, therefore, state-wise data is not maintained for the EVs incentivised under the scheme. An amount of Rs.2,000 crore has been allocated under the scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS).  As on 01.07.2026, an amount of Rs.689 crore has been approved for deployment of 6,562 chargers to 3 Oil Marketing Companies and 9 States. Further, 14,000 e-buses have been allocated under the scheme out of which Letters of Confirmation of Demand (LoCD) have been issued to respective cities/STUs and Letters of Confirmation of Quantity (LoCQ) have also been issued to the successful bidders for 13,800 e-buses. Surat and Hyderabad have signed concession agreement for 600 and 915 electric buses, respectively. The selected bidders are required to get their e-bus prototype approved and deploy the buses. -3- (c): No such assessment has been done, however, EV penetration levels have gone up from 0.7% in FY 2019-20 to 8.2% in FY 2025-26, supported by PM E-DRIVE, FAME-II and other government schemes/policies. Promotion of domestic manufacturing: OEMs registered under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme have localised their EV models under PM E-DRIVE scheme and have obtained certificates of compliance to Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP) for their EV models from testing agencies of MHI. (d): An Allocation of Rs. 2,000 crore has been made for deployment of adequate number of EVPCS on pan India basis.  As on 01.07.2026, an amount of Rs.689 crore has been approved for deployment of 6,562 chargers to 3 Oil Marketing Companies and 9 States. The Government has implemented Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, ‘National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cells (ACC) Battery Storage’ from 12 th May, 2021 with a total budgetary outlay of Rs.18,100 crore for manufacturing of ACC in the country.  The scheme envisages to establish a competitive ACC battery manufacturing set up in the country for 50 GWh. Further, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MOEFCC) has notified Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, dated 22 nd August 2022 for environmental factors. (e): The PM E-DRIVE scheme has been implemented on pan India basis including Tier-II and Tier-III cities and aspirational regions to promote wider adoption of electric mobility and support the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. ******* TPJ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290696) आगंतुक पटल  : 156 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Heavy Industries PM E-DRIVE SCHEME AND PROMOTION OF ELECTRIC MOBILITY प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: The PM E-DRIVE Scheme has been implemented on pan India basis and no state-wise allocation has been done under the scheme
content:

                28 JUL 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi (a): The PM E-DRIVE Scheme has been implemented on pan India basis and no state-wise allocation has been done under the scheme.  The incentives are provided to eligible electric vehicle buyers in the form of an upfront reduction in the purchase price, which is subsequently reimbursed to the Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI). In view of the same, the details of total funds allocated versus utilized under PM E-DRIVE for FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27, and the claims currently pending reimbursement under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme as on 22/07/2026 is as under : - Table : Status of Funds allocated under PM E-DRIVE Scheme in FY 25-26 & 26-27 and actual utilization till 22.07.2026 Rs. crore Fund Allocated Actual Expenditure Claims pending for Disbursement (under processing) FY 2025-26 1,300 1,160.32 - FY 2026-27 1,500 169.06 (as on 22.07.2026) 139.43 (b): Users may at times experience portal friction due to network issues, anti-virus scanning or urgent maintenance activity by NIC, or Aadhaar authentication issues as mentioned below : 1.           The mobile number used for face authentication was not linked with the beneficiary's Aadhaar. 2.           Aadhaar biometric authentication could not be completed due to outdated or mismatched biometric records, requiring beneficiaries to update their biometrics. title: Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) Scheme Phase-II
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Heavy Industries Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) Scheme Phase-II प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi (a): Yes. (b): No National Electric Vehicle Policy or National Framework is under consideration in the Ministry of Heavy Industries. (c) & (d): Question does not arise in view of part (b). (e): The Schemes being implemented by the Government for the development of a balanced and coordinated EV eco-system across the country are as under: (i) Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) Scheme Phase-II : The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme provided demand incentive for e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting up of EV public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh electric vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e-4Ws. In addition, 5,197 electric buses (e-buses) have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country. (ii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of ₹25,938 crore. (iii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage : The Government on 09.06.2021 notified the PLI  Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries. (iv) PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore has been notified on 29.09.2024. This scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e-Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public charging stations (EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. title: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Heavy Industries Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto) प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi The following schemes are administered by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) to promote domestic manufacturing and technological upgradation: (i) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government approved this scheme on 23.09.2021 for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products with a budgetary outlay of Rs. 25,938 crore. The scheme provides financial incentives on manufacturing of AAT products including EVs with minimum 50% Domestic Value Addition (DVA) and attract investments in the automotive manufacturing value chain. The Scheme has attracted an investment of Rs. 44,326 Crore and generated employment of 67,820 till 31.03.2026. Further, under the Scheme, expenditures incurred by beneficiary firms on Research and Development (R&D) are permitted to meet investment criteria, allowing them to integrate the latest technology in the implementation of their projects. (ii)        Production Linked Incentive Scheme on National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage: The Government on 12.05.2021 approved PLI Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of Rs.18,100 crore. The scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries, out of which 40 GWh ACC capacity has been awarded to four beneficiary firms. Under the Scheme, a Giga-Scale ACC manufacturing plant with an installed capacity of 1.4 GWh has been established. The scheme has attracted an investment of ₹5,180 crore and direct employment of 1,277 till 31.05.2026. Further, under the Scheme, expenditures incurred by beneficiary firms on Research and Development (R&D) are permitted to meet investment criteria, allowing them to integrate the latest technology in the implementation of their projects. (iii) PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) Scheme: This scheme has been approved with an outlay of Rs. 10,900 crore w.e.f. 01.04.2024 till 31.03.2028. The scheme supports domestic manufacturing of electric vehicles including e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e-Ambulances. The scheme also supports EV public charging stations and upgradation of testing agencies. (iv) Scheme on Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector- Phase-II: This Scheme has the objective to encourage technology development and strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities. Under one of the component of the Scheme, i.e., “Common Engineering Facility Centres”, MHI has set up 4 Smart Advanced Manufacturing and Rapid Transformation Hub (SAMARTH) Centres to promote Industry 4.0. MHI has also sanctioned setting up of 10 cluster Industry 4.0 Experience Centres nationwide through Centre for Industry 4.0 (C4i4), Pune at a project cost of Rs. 35 crore. In order to support digital manufacturing, MHI has approved project named ‘Augmentation of Centre of Excellence by Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore’ with total project cost of Rs. 44.6 crore and project named ‘Development of Laser-based directed energy deposition additive manufacturing machine’ by Central Manufacturing Technology Institute (CMTI) with project cost of Rs. 4.943 crore. -3- In addition to the above Schemes, MHI has notified 'Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet' having financial outlay of Rs. 7280 crore, with the aim to establish 6,000 Metric Tons per annum (MTPA) of sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM) manufacturing in India, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the global REPM market. (d): As informed by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), to facilitate Investment, foster Innovation, build best in class Infrastructure, and make India a hub for manufacturing, design, and innovation, ‘Make in India’ initiative was launched on 25 th September 2014. Presently, Make in India 2.0 focuses on 27 sectors including 15 manufacturing sectors, implemented across various Ministries and Departments and State Governments. Further, Government has taken a series of policy initiatives that include the Atmanirbhar Bharat packages, investment opportunities under National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) and National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP), India Industrial Land Bank (IILB), Industrial Park Rating System (IPRS), soft launch of the National Single Window System (NSWS), etc. to promote manufacturing. (e): No such proposal has been received by this Ministry. ******* TPJ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290691) आगंतुक पटल  : 51 Ministry of Heavy Industries Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto) प्रविष्टि तिथि:
