title: FUNDS TO NFIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs FUNDS TO NFIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has approved the National Forensic Infrastructure Enhancement Scheme (NFIES) with a total financial outlay of ₹2254.43 crore from financial year 2024-25 to 2028-29. Under the scheme, ₹1309.13 crore have been allocated for setting up of 09 campuses of the National Forensic  Sciences  University  (NFSU) and ₹860.3 crore for setting up of 07 Central Forensic Science Laboratories (CFSLs). Funds to the tune of ₹119.09 crore have been released and utilized under the scheme for the NFSU campuses and for CFSLs. The Scheme is being implemented centrally for creation and strengthening of forensic infrastructure at identified locations. Under the scheme, setting up of 09 campuses of the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) has been approved in Nagpur (Maharashtra), Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Khordha (Odisha), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu), Rajasthan, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal. Further, setting up of 07 Central Forensic Science Laboratories (CFSLs) has also been approved in Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Khordha (Odisha), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu), Rajasthan, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Kerala. 06 CFSLs at Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar are to be co - located with the NFSU campus. So far, land for NFSU campus / CFSL has been allotted in Nagpur (Maharashtra), Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Khordha (Odisha), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu) and Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh). The NFSU campuses are currently operational from Transit buildings allotted in Nagpur (Maharashtra), Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Khordha (Odisha), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu), and Jaipur (Rajasthan). title: CELL BROADCAST ALERT SYSTEM FOR DISASTER WARNINGS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs CELL BROADCAST ALERT SYSTEM FOR DISASTER WARNINGS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi Cell Broadcast Alert System for Disaster Warnings is operated through the Integrated Alert System based on the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) implemented by National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). The system   integrates   five   Warning   Generating   Agencies,  namely the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission (CWC), Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment (DGRE) and Forest Survey of India (FSI), with the State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs) of all States/UTs. The respective Warning Generating Agencies and SDMAs are responsible for issuing and authorising disaster-specific alerts, while the CAP-based platform facilitates their dissemination through the Cell Broadcast system. The Cell Broadcast Alert will be used for timely warning to citizens for disaster events with very short lead time like Cyclone, Tsunami, Heavy Rainfall, Lightning, Flash Flood, Thunderstorms, Hailstorm, Avalanche, Cloudburst, Industrial/man-made disasters and other events which merit immediate alerting. The Warning generating agencies provide Geo-targeted warnings and Geo-targeted alerts are disseminated to the public. Timely receipt of warning and timely dissemination of alerts acts as one of the contributing factor in reducing disaster-related causalities and improving emergency preparedness. The System provides timely alerts to the public, which indirectly improves emergency preparedness and necessary precautions, thus helps in reducing disaster-related casualties. All warnings generated by the forecasting agencies are translated to the State language of the target population and disseminated to the recipients by the SDMAs. The Alerts are received across all mobile networks and handsets in the geo-targeted area which includes remote and vulnerable areas. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. ***** RK/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290380) आगंतुक पटल  : 143 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali Ministry of Home Affairs CELL BROADCAST ALERT SYSTEM FOR DISASTER WARNINGS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: NATIONAL DRUG CONTROL VISION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs NATIONAL DRUG CONTROL VISION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:24PM by PIB Delhi To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) has been released on 26.06.2026. The Vision Document is to be implemented by the concerned Central Ministries/ Departments/ agencies and the State Governments/UTs as per the action points and timelines specifically mentioned for each Central Ministry/ Department/ Agency. The four key focus areas outlined in the Vision Document are as under: - Enforcement (Intelligence & Operations) Precursors & Synthetic Drugs Control Demand & Harm Reduction Capacity Building & Coordination Specific actionable points for the States/UTs including State of Assam and Andhra Pradesh along with the timelines have been   detailed in the Vision Document. It is further envisaged that States and Districts would prepare their vision for 3 years Road Map to control drugs in consonance with the National Road Map outlined in the Vision Document. The Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026–2029) envisages a comprehensive framework for capacity building, awareness and preventive interventions. It focuses on strengthening the institutional capacity of States, Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTFs), forensic laboratories and NCB, enhancing inter-agency coordination through the Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism. Further, under Demand and Harm Reduction, the Vision Document seeks to strengthen the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) through large-scale awareness and preventive initiatives in educational institutions and communities, including awareness campaigns, training of teachers, counsellors and healthcare professionals, promotion of drug-free campuses, consent based screening as part of student welfare programme, establishment of Anti-Drug Committees, appointment of anti-drug officers and institutional mechanisms for early identification, counselling and referral of students, through various Ministries in the Government. The Vision Document envisages training of law enforcement officers, forensic experts, healthcare professionals, teachers, sensitization of students and judicial officers on drug abuse prevention. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. ***** RK/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290379) आगंतुक पटल  : 142 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Assamese Ministry of Home Affairs NATIONAL DRUG CONTROL VISION प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: CFCFRMS 2.0 PLATFORM
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs CFCFRMS 2.0 PLATFORM प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:20PM by PIB Delhi The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ (CFCFRMS), under Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters. As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30.06.2026, financial amount of more than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 lakh complaints.  A toll-free Helpline number ‘1930’ has been operationalized to get assistance in lodging online cyber complaints. To further strengthen operational efficiency and ensure uniformity in handling cybercrime complaints, the Ministry has issued a comprehensive Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for NCRP-CFCFRMS. The SOP lays down a standardized framework for complaint processing, bank coordination, grievance redressal, removal of lien markings, and restoration of defrauded funds to rightful claimants based on complaints received through the NCRP. Money Restoration Module for expeditious restoration of defrauded money to the victims and Grievance Redressal Module for timely attending to the grievances relating to freezing of the bank accounts and lien marking of the amount, have been made functional from April, 2026. ‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule  of  the    Constitution   of   India.    The  States/UTs   are  primarily responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation, and prosecution of crimes including establishment of cyber forensic laboratories through their Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs). The Central Government supplements the initiatives of the States/UTs through advisories and financial assistance under various schemes for capacity building of their LEAs. Cyber crime incidents reported on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, their conversion into FIRs and subsequent action i.e. filing of chargesheets, arrest and resolution of complaints, thereon are handled by the State/UT Law Enforcement Agencies concerned as per the provisions of the law. A Suspect Registry of identifiers of cyber criminals has been launched by I4C on 10.09.2024 in collaboration with Banks/Financial Institutions. Till 30.06.2026, more than 30.48 lakh suspect identifier data received from Banks and 32.08 lakh Layer 1 mule accounts have been shared with the participating entities of Suspect Registry and declined transactions worth Rs. 25,698 crores. CERT-In issues alerts and advisories regarding latest cyber threats/vulnerabilities      including     malicious    attacks    using    Artificial Intelligence and countermeasures to protect computers, networks and data on an ongoing basis. AI driven situational awareness systems are deployed by CERT-In to detect malicious domains and phishing activities for necessary mitigation. CERT-In operates an automated cyber threat intelligence exchange platform for sharing tailored alerts with organisations across sectors for proactive threat mitigation. The Ministry of Home Affairs has released financial assistance  to the tune of Rs. 132.93 crores under the ‘Cyber Crime Prevention against Women and Children (CCPWC)’ Scheme, to the States/UTs for their capacity building such as setting up of cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories, hiring of junior cyber consultants and training of LEAs’ personnel, public prosecutors and judicial officers. Cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories have been commissioned in 33 States/UTs including Maharashtra and more than 24,600 LEAs personnel, judicial officers and prosecutors have been provided training on cyber crime awareness, investigation, forensics etc. The state of the art National-Digital Investigation Support Centre (previously   known   as  National  Cyber  Forensic Laboratory (Investigation) {NCFL(I)}) has been established, as a part of the I4C, at New Delhi (on 18.02.2019) and at Assam  (on 29.08.2025) to provide  early stage cyber  forensic assistance to Investigating Officers (IOs) of State/UT Police. Till 30.06.2026, National-Digital Investigation Support Centre, New Delhi has provided its services to State/UT LEAs in more than 14,064 cases pertaining to cyber crimes. At present, 07 Central Forensic Science Laboratories and 28 State Forensic Science Laboratories including in Maharashtra are operational across the country to assist in investigation of cybercrime cases. Assistance has been provided to 20 States / UTs for Strengthening of Cyber Forensic Capacities in State FSLs under the Nirbhaya funded scheme for Strengthening of DNA Analysis and Cyber Forensic Capacities in State FSLs. Till 30.06.2026, a total of 1,586 entities have been onboarded onto the CFCFRMS platform, including 40 foreign banks operating in India. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. ***** RK/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290377) आगंतुक पटल  : 166 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Home Affairs CFCFRMS 2.0 PLATFORM प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: KHADI PRODUCTS TO CAPF
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs KHADI PRODUCTS TO CAPF प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:19PM by PIB Delhi In order to promote the procurement and daily use of  Swadeshi and Khadi products, Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) has been registered with Kendriya Police Kalyan Bhandar (KPKB) since 13th March 2020. Also a  number of steps have been taken in the direction:- (i)  Four items, i.e (i) Mustard Oil (ii) Cotton Bed Durries (iii) Woolen Blanket and (iv) Bed Sheet and Pillow Cover have been identified for procurement by CAPFs from Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC). (ii)      ITBP is the Nodal Force for procurement of Mustard Oil and Durries. CRPF is the Nodal Force for procurement of Blankets, and ADG (Medical), CAPFs, is the Nodal for the procurement of Bed Sheet and Pillow Cover. (iii)     Swadeshi and Khadi products are also being sold through Master Bhandars and Subsidiary Bhandars of KPKB for the benefit of serving and retired personnel of CAPFs all over India. (iv)     Daily use items are procured by the CAPFs from the KVIC. (v)      The National Bee Board is continuously providing necessary support and training to all forces for scientific beekeeping. Gardens are being developed within the premises of the Central Armed Police Forces by planting more flowering plants to create a suitable environment for honey production. Honey produced through beekeeping is being used as food for the soldiers to enhance their health and immunity. Under Vibrant Village Programme-II (VVP-II), CAPFs have started procuring edible items such as fruits, vegetables, dairy products, dry rations and meats from Self-Help Groups (SHGs) & State Cooperative Societies of border areas. The comprehensive details of the Civic Action Programme (CAP) allocations and welfare activities conducted by the CAPFs in border areas are given at annexure-I. In addition to above, allocations and welfare activities conducted CAP particularly in Darjeeling and Kalimpong districts are given at annexure II & III respectively. ANNEXURE - I Repairs to community buildings, viz, schools, hospitals, health centers, community hall etc. Constructions of tracks, small bridges, culverts, mines, cableway, water supply, electrification schemes, playground etc. Running of health, medical, dental, veterinary camps which include providing of medical equipment and stores etc. to existing hospitals nursing homes. Human Resources Development to include imparting of vocational training, conduct of educational excursions to students to places of national interest and to organize career counseling training and coaching etc. Initiation of small projects in improvement and care of livestock, beekeepeing, fisheries, agricultural techniques, orchards, forestry carpet and or handloom weaving, history etc. Sanitation and Hygiene through Extension Services and social education. Drinking water basic precaution and system of storage. Development of sources of non-conventional energy. Development of handicraft and cottage industries. Assistance during Natural Calamities. Water harvesting structure. Sports facilities. Distribution of Transistor. Pre-recruitment training. title: VIBRANT VILLAGE PROGRAMME
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs VIBRANT VILLAGE PROGRAMME प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi The Government has approved Vibrant Villages Programme-I (VVP-I) as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme on 15 th February, 2023 for comprehensive development of the select villages in 46 blocks abutting northern border in 19 districts in   the  States of   Arunachal Pradesh,  Himachal  Pradesh,  Sikkim, Uttarakhand and UT of Ladakh. Since the launch of the Vibrant Villages Programme-I (VVP-I) in 2023, 832 Projects in Arunachal Pradesh, 98 in Himachal Pradesh, 79 in Ladakh (UT), 87 in Sikkim and 152 in Uttarakhand have been sanctioned under the programme by MHA with an outlay of ₹3065.32 Crore. As reported by the States/UT, 316 projects have been completed as on date. Further, 1658 projects have been sanctioned by the Central Ministries/Departments under convergence. Under VVP-I, 662 villages have been identified for comprehensive development on priority, comprising 455 villages in Arunachal Pradesh, 46 in Sikkim, 51 in Uttarakhand, 75 in Himachal Pradesh and 35 in the UT of Ladakh. An amount of ₹953.47 crore has been released to the States/UT under the programme. Under VVP-I, 111 road projects with an outlay of ₹2,481.93 crore have been sanctioned for providing all-weather road connectivity to 134 unconnected villages. As informed by the Ministries/Departments/State Governments, 528 villages are connected with 4G mobile connectivity, 625 villages are covered with piped drinking water supply and 621 villages have access to on-grid/off-grid electricity. In addition, MHA has sanctioned 140 off-grid solar projects and 7 micro-hydel projects under VVP-I. Under convergence, Ministry of Power has sanctioned 43 projects with an outlay of ₹238.30 crore for augmentation of power distribution infrastructure. 40 Mobile Medical Units have been sanctioned under VVP-I for health services in Arunachal Pradesh. 146 projects for construction/ upgradation of school infrastructure have been sanctioned under the programme. The implementation of projects under Vibrant Villages Programme-I (VVP-I) is reviewed periodically. Necessary coordination with the Ministries/Departments concerned and the State Governments/UT Administration is undertaken wherever required to facilitate implementation. No third-party evaluation has been conducted under Vibrant Villages Programme-I (VVP-I). This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. ***** RK/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290369) आगंतुक पटल  : 200 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Tamil Ministry of Home Affairs VIBRANT VILLAGE PROGRAMME प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: CYBER CRIME MITIGATION CENTRE
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs CYBER CRIME MITIGATION CENTRE प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:16PM by PIB Delhi ‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. The States/UTs are primarily responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation, and prosecution of crimes including cyber fraud through their Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs). The Central Government supplements the initiatives of the States/UTs through advisories and financial assistance under various schemes for capacity building of their LEAs. To strengthen the mechanism to deal with cyber crimes including cyber financial fraud in a comprehensive and coordinated manner, the Central Government has taken steps which, inter-alia, include the following: The Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre’ (I4C) as an attached office to deal with all types of cyber crimes in the country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner. The ‘National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal’ (NCRP) (https://cybercrime.gov.in) has been launched, as a part of the I4C, to enable public to report incidents pertaining to all types of cyber crimes, with special focus on cyber crimes against women and children. The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ (CFCFRMS), under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters. As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30.06.2026, financial amount of more than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 lakh complaints.  A toll-free Helpline number ‘1930’ has been operationalized to get assistance in lodging online cyber complaints. A State of the Art, Cyber Fraud Mitigation Centre (CFMC) has been established at I4C where representatives of major banks, Financial Intermediaries, Payment Aggregators, Telecom Service Providers, IT Intermediaries and representatives of States/UTs Law Enforcement Agency are working together for immediate action and seamless cooperation to tackle cybercrime. Till 30.06.2026, more than 15.75 lakhs SIM cards and 5.77 lakhs IMEIs as reported by Police authorities have been blocked by Government of India. A Suspect Registry of identifiers of cyber criminals has been launched by I4C on 10.09.2024 in collaboration with Banks/Financial Institutions. Till 30.06.2026, more than 30.48 lakh suspect identifier data received from Banks and 32.08 lakh Layer 1 mule accounts have been shared with the participating entities of Suspect Registry and declined transactions worth Rs. 25,698 crores. Samanvaya Platform has been made operational to serve as an Management Information System (MIS) platform, data repository and a coordination platform for LEAs for cybercrime data sharing and analytics. It provides analytics based interstate linkages of crimes and criminals, involved in cybercrime complaints in various States/UTs. The module ‘Pratibimb’ maps locations of criminals and crime infrastructure on a map to give visibility to jurisdictional officers. The module also facilitates seeking and receiving of techno-legal assistance by Law Enforcement  Agencies from I4C and other SMEs. It has lead to arrest of more than 29,837 accused and more than 2,33,593 Cyber Investigation assistance request. ‘Sahyog’ Portal has been launched to expedite the process of sending notices  to  IT  intermediaries  by  the  Appropriate  Government  or  its agency under clause (b) of sub-section (3) of section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 to facilitate the removal or disabling of access to any information, data or communication link being used to commit an unlawful act. The Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC) platform, namely ‘CyTrain’ portal has been developed under I4C, for capacity building of police officers/judicial officers through online course on critical aspects of cyber crime investigation, forensics, prosecution etc. Till 30.06.2026, more than 1,63,344 police officers/judicial officers from States/UTs are registered and more than 1,61,957 Certificates issued through the portal. Cyber Commando programme was launched by the Hon'ble Home Minister on 10.09.2024 to establish a Special Wing of Cyber Commandos equipped with specialized training to counter cybersecurity threats in the country. The programme envisions the creation of a dedicated, skilled workforce capable of securing critical information infrastructure and supporting national cybersecurity efforts. 281 cyber commandos successfully completed training. I4C, MHA is regularly organising ‘State Connect’, ‘Thana Connect’ ‘Bank Connect’ and Peer learning session to share best practices, enhance capacity building, etc. The state of the art National-Digital Investigation Support Centre (previously    known     as     National    Cyber     Forensic     Laboratory (Investigation)  {NCFL(I)}) has been established, as a part of the I4C, at New Delhi (on 18.02.2019) and at Assam (on 29.08.2025) to provide early stage cyber forensic assistance to Investigating Officers (IOs) of State/UT Police. Till 30.06.2026, National-Digital Investigation Support Centre, New Delhi has provided its services to State/UT LEAs in more than 14,064 cases pertaining to cyber crimes. To further strengthen operational efficiency and ensure uniformity in handling cybercrime complaints, the Ministry has issued a comprehensive Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for NCRP-CFCFRMS. The SOP lays down a standardized framework for complaint processing, bank coordination, grievance redressal, removal of lien markings, and restoration of defrauded funds to rightful claimants based on complaints received through the NCRP. Money Restoration Module for expeditious restoration of defrauded money to the victims and Grievance Redressal Module for timely attending to the grievances relating to freezing of the bank accounts and lien marking of the amount, have been made functional from April, 2026. To further spread awareness on cyber crime, the Central Government has taken steps which, inter-alia, include; caller tune campaign, dissemination of messages through SMS, I4C social media account i.e. X (formerly Twitter) (@CyberDost),          Facebook(CyberDostI4C),         Instagram (CyberDostI4C), Telegram(cyberdosti4c), SMS campaign, TV campaign, Radio campaign, School Campaign, advertisement in cinema halls, celebrity endorsement, IPL campaign, engaged MyGov for publicity in multiple mediums,  organizing Cyber Safety and Security Awareness weeks in association with States/UTs, digital displays on metro stations, railway stations and airports across, etc. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290366) आगंतुक पटल  : 232 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Home Affairs CYBER CRIME MITIGATION CENTRE प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: JUSTICE CENTRIC SYSTEM
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs JUSTICE CENTRIC SYSTEM प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi The new Sanhitas mark a significant step towards creating a citizen centric, more accessible and efficient justice system. The main provisions made in the new Sanhitas that focus on justice rather than punishment are given in the Annexure. In the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, stringent punishment up to death sentence has been provided for the offence of rape of a minor. The offence of gang rape on a minor is punishable with imprisonment for life or death. Details of the main provisions in the New Sanhitas that focus on Justice rather than punishment: (A) Victim Centric Provisions Report Incidents Online: A person may now report incidents by electronic communication, without the need to physically visit a police station. This allows for easier and quicker reporting, facilitating prompt action by the police. File FIR at Any Police Station: With the introduction of Zero FIR, a person can file a First Information Report (FIR) at any police station, regardless of jurisdiction. This eliminates delays in initiating legal proceedings and ensures immediate reporting of the offence. Free Copy of FIR: Victim is entitled to receive a free copy of the FIR, ensuring their participation in the legal process. Right to Inform Upon Arrest: In the event of an arrest, the individual has the right to inform a person of his choice about their situation. This will ensure immediate support and assistance to the arrested individual. Display of Arrest Information:  Every police station and district must now have a designated police officer not below the rank of ASI and the information of all arrested individuals shall now be prominently displayed in every police station. This safeguards the right of the accused persons and mitigates instances of custodial violence and illegal detention by police. Progress Updates to Victims: Victims are entitled to get update on the progress of their case within 90 days. This provision keeps victims informed and involved in the legal process, enhancing transparency and trust. Supply of police report and other documents: Both the accused and the victim are entitled to receive copies of the FIR, police report/chargesheet, statements, confessions and other documents within 14 days. Witness Protection Scheme: The new laws mandate all State Governments to implement Witness Protection Scheme to ensure the safety and security of witnesses, enhancing the credibility and effectiveness of legal proceedings. Exemption from going to police station: Women, persons below 15 years, persons above 60 years, and those with disabilities or acute illness are exempt from attending police stations. It is mandated that victim be heard before withdrawal from prosecution in Section 360 of BNSS. The statutory recognition of the right of the victim to be heard is a significant example of a nyaya centric approach to criminal justice system. By mandatorily hearing the victim in proceedings regarding withdrawal of cases, the justice system becomes more responsive to the needs and concerns of those directly affected by crime. (B) Timelines Faster and Fair Resolution:  The new laws promise a faster and fair resolution of cases, instilling confidence in the legal system. Crucial stages of investigation and trial like - preliminary enquiry (to be completed in 14 days), further investigation (to be completed in 90 days), supply of document to the victim and accused (within 14 days), commitment of a case for trial (within 90 days), filing of discharge applications (within 60 days), framing of charges (within 60 days), pronouncement   of judgment   (within 45 days)   and   filing   of  mercy petitions (30 days before Governor and 60 days before President) - have been streamlined and to be completed within stipulated time period. Fast-Track Investigations: The new laws prioritized the investigations for offences against women and children, ensuring timely completion within two months of recording information. Limited Adjournments:  Courts can grant a maximum of two adjournments to avoid unnecessary delays in case hearings, ensuring timely justice delivery. (C) Reformative Approach i. Community service: The new laws introduce community service for minor offences. The offenders get the chance to positively contribute to society, learn from their mistakes and build stronger community bonds. ii. Expansion of the ambit of summary trial: The ambit of summary trial has now been expanded to include more offences ensuring expeditious disposal of cases. (D) Rights of the Accused Arbitrary arrest of individuals solely to initiate judicial proceedings has been curtailed. The police, now, need not arrest an accused person just for the Magistrate to take cognizance of the police report and no arrest is needed for taking handwriting, signature, fingerprint, or voice samples. (E)     Trial in absentia A new provision of trial in absentia for persons declared as proclaimed offenders allows the Court to proceed with the trial and pronounce the verdict in the absence of the accused. This provision ensures that justice is neither delayed nor denied. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290363) आगंतुक पटल  : 153 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Home Affairs JUSTICE CENTRIC SYSTEM प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: The National SC-ST Hub Scheme is helping in reliable supply chains, increased employment generation and participation of SC/ST entrepreneurs in India's industrial ecosystem
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises The National SC-ST Hub Scheme is helping in reliable supply chains, increased employment generation and participation of SC/ST entrepreneurs in India's industrial ecosystem NSSH is Empowering SC-ST Entrepreneurs: Enabling Technology, Capacity and Market Access for Inclusive Growth प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi The National SC-ST Hub Scheme (NSSH) scheme, under the Ministry of MSME, continues to strengthen the competitiveness of SC-ST entrepreneurs by enabling technology upgradation, enhancing business capabilities and facilitating greater participation in public procurement. Through interventions such as the Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) and the Business Acceleration Programme (BAP), the scheme is helping enterprises overcome operational constraints, adopt modern technologies, augment compliance and access larger institutional markets. Engineering Excellence through Technology Upgradation: The Journey of Varun Enterprises, Punjab Led by Mr. Hukum Chand, Varun Enterprises has established a strong presence in the engineering and manufacturing sector by delivering reliable, high-quality industrial solutions. With focus on precision, quality and compliance, the enterprise steadily built its capabilities to meet the requirements of institutional and Government buyers. Overcoming Capacity Constraints As the enterprise expands, adopting advanced technology became essential to enhance productivity, reduce turnaround time and remain competitive in an evolving market. Hence, with support from the National SC-ST Hub Office, Ludhiana, Varun Enterprises availed ₹15.67 lakh under the SCLCSS during 2021-22. This support enabled the installation of advanced manufacturing equipment, including a fibre laser cutting system, CNC hydraulic press brake, air compressor, UPS systems and supporting electrical infrastructure. The upgraded machines significantly enhanced production efficiency, precision, quality and operational reliability, enabling the enterprise to participate in larger procurement. A significant milestone was securing a ₹95.99 lakh purchase order from the Modern Coach Factory (MCF), Rae Bareli, for supply of connection boxes in rail coaches. This achievement reinforced the enterprise's credibility as a reliable supplier capable of delivering quality engineering solutions for the railways. Positioning for Long-Term Growth With modern manufacturing capabilities, Varun Enterprises has positioned its footprint in high-value engineering products. title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Makes Rooftop Solar Accessible for All with Subsidy Support and Low-Interest Financing
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of New and Renewable Energy PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Makes Rooftop Solar Accessible for All with Subsidy Support and Low-Interest Financing प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi In order to ensure the affordability of rooftop solar (RTS) systems for middle-income and economically weaker households under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY), following provisions have been made: Higher central financial assistance for the first two kWp of RTS capacity. Availability of collateral-free loan from nationalized banks at a concessional interest rate of repo-rate plus 50 bps, i.e., 5.75% per annum for the present, with a tenure of 10 years. Included RESCO/Utility-Led Aggregation (ULA) Models. The year-wise budgetary allocation and funds released under the PMSG: MBY is given below: - FY Budget Estimates (Rs. Cr.) Expenditure Incurred (Rs. Cr.) 2024-25 6,250 7,822.92 2025-26 20,000 16,166.23 2026-27 22000 10,392.48 (as on 22.7.2026) As a result of various the measures taken to accelerate the deployment of RTS systems under the scheme, a total of 39,72,447 RTS system has been installed covering 48,02,717 households as on 22.7.2026. While the electricity bills of consumers installed RTS under the scheme have been largely reduced, over 18.93 households reported even zero electricity bills for some months, depending on their self-consumption of electricity. title: Centre Promotes Convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar Schemes to Accelerate Solar Adoption and Rural Energy Self-Sufficiency
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Centre Promotes Convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar Schemes to Accelerate Solar Adoption and Rural Energy Self-Sufficiency प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:40PM by PIB Delhi Government has been promoting convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana with suitable Central and State programmes and funding sources, wherever feasible, to facilitate wider adoption of the schemes. For instance, PM KUSUM scheme guidelines allow for convergence with other central schemes including: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) scheme for access of easy financing Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) for solarization of segregated agriculture feeders Promotion of micro irrigation techniques and Per Drop More Crop scheme Replacement of agriculture pumps with energy efficient pumps Gram Urja Swaraj Campaign to enhance self-sufficiency at village level Similarly for PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, the convergence is taken up with Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), for implementing the Solar Didi Programme under which women Self-Help Group (SHG) members under DAY-NULM are trained. Convergence of District Mineral Foundation (DMF) funds is also encouraged with PM Surya Ghar for eligible beneficiaries, particularly BPL households, PMAY beneficiaries and other vulnerable sections. The Ministry has already issued communications and possible areas of convergence to all the states for convergence of PM KUSUM and PMSG Schemes with scheme of Ministry of Cooperation, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Rural Development etc. This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha. ***** Nihi Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290403) आगंतुक पटल  : 190 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Kannada Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Centre Promotes Convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar Schemes to Accelerate Solar Adoption and Rural Energy Self-Sufficiency प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
title: Over 48 Lakh Households Benefit Under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Since February 2024
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Over 48 Lakh Households Benefit Under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Since February 2024 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 3:39PM by PIB Delhi The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY) is a demand-driven scheme wherein all residential consumers in the country including the rural households, having a grid-connected electricity connection with the local DISCOM, can avail the benefits of the scheme, for installation of rooftop solar (RTS) systems by applying on the National Portal ( www.pmsuryaghar.gov.in ) of the scheme. During the year 2025-26, a total of 18. 71 lakh RTS systems have been installed with a cumulative installed solar capacity of 6.7 GW, benefitting 22.71 lakh households across the country, including the rural households under the PMSG: MBY. Under the PMSG: MBY, since its launch in February 2024, a total of 39,72,447 RTS systems have been installed, benefitting 48,02,717 households across the country including the households in rural areas, as on 22.07.2026. While the electricity bills of consumers installed RTS under the scheme have been largely reduced, over 18.93 lakh beneficiaries have been reported by DISCOMs across the country , including the rural households to receive zero electricity bill after installation of RTS systems under the scheme during the any month/billing period , depending on their self-consumption of electricity. Apart from installation of rooftop solar plants in residential sector, the PMSG: MBY also envisage installation of RTS plants in Government and commercial buildings including educational and health institutions, however, no central financial assistance (CFA) is provided to these categories of consumers as installation of rooftop solar plants is financially viable for them even without CFA. This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha. ***** Nihi Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290402) आगंतुक पटल  : 186 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Kannada , Gujarati , Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Tamil Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Over 48 Lakh Households Benefit Under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Since February 2024 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Panchayati Raj GRANTS TO PRIS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 5:01PM by PIB Delhi The details of tied grants, untied grants, and performance-linked grants recommended under the 16th Finance Commission for Panchayati Raj Institutions, State-wise are attached at Annexure-I. The Central Finance Commission grants for Rural Local Bodies are not recommended for Union Territories. The criteria relating to the uploading of audited accounts and increase in own revenues over the preceding year, were applicable for availing Performance Grants for the period 2016-17 to 2019-20 under the 14th Finance Commission. Accordingly, the State/UT-wise details of Performance Grants released to States, including Chhattisgarh, in respect of all eligible Gram Panchayats under the 14th Finance Commission are given at Annexure-II. However, this Ministry does not maintain Gram Panchayat–wise details. Further, there was no Performance Grant component under the 15th Finance Commission during award period 2020-21 to 2025-26. Under the 10 th (FYs 1995-2000) and 11 th (FYs 2000-2005) Finance Commission, a total grants of Rs. 3576.35 Crore out of total allocation of 4380.93 Crore and Rs.6601.85 Crore out of the total allocation Rs.8000.00 Crore respectively were released for the Panchayati Raj Institutions. However, the state-wise details in this regard are not available with the Ministry. Further, the State-wise details of grants recommended, grants actually released under 12 th to 15 th Finance Commission to Panchayati Raj Institutions are given at Annexure-III to Annexure-VI. Meanwhile, States/UTs wise current status of elections of Panchayati Raj Institutions is given at Annexure-VII. Panchayat, being a “Local Self Government”, is a State subject and part of the State List of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Accordingly, strengthening Panchayat capacity is primarily the responsibility of States/UTs. However, the Ministry is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely the Revamped Rashtriya Gram SwarajAbhiyan (RGSA), w.e.f. financial year 2022-23, with the objective of supporting Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by imparting training to Elected Representatives (ERs) and other stakeholders to develop leadership abilities, thereby enabling Gram Panchayats to function effectively across all States/UTs. Under the scheme, capacity-building support is provided to elected representatives, functionaries, and other stakeholders of Panchayats across different categories, viz. basic orientation and refresher programmes, thematic interventions, specialized training, and Panchayat Development Plan-related programmes, etc. Under this scheme, 6,16,642 participants were provided training in the State of Chhattisgarh, during 2022-23 to 2026-27 (as on 10.07.2026). title: EMPOWERMENT OF PANCHAYATI RAJ INSTITUTIONS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Panchayati Raj EMPOWERMENT OF PANCHAYATI RAJ INSTITUTIONS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:56PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has released a report titled “Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States - An Indicative Evidence-Based Ranking, 2024” in February 2025 to assess the effectiveness of devolution and the role of local governments in strengthening grassroots democracy, including assessment of the status of financial and administrative empowerment of Panchayats Raj Institutions (PRIs). This report presents the Devolution Index, which provides the overall scores and ranks for all States/Union Territories (UTs) covered under Part-IX of the Constitution, based on six identified dimensions: Framework, Functions, Finances, Functionaries, Capacity Enhancement, and Accountability. Many Gram Panchayats are facing difficulties in effectively implementing local development works due to inadequate financial resources, shortage of manpower and limited administrative powers. “Panchayat”, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of State List of Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Panchayats are set up and operate through the respective State Panchayati Raj Acts which may vary from State to State, subject to the provisions of the Constitution. Article 243G of the Constitution empowers the Legislature of a State to make provisions, by law, for the devolution of power and responsibilities upon Panchayat at the appropriate level, subject to such conditions as may be specified, with respect to the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and implementation of schemes for economic development and social justice as may be entrusted to them including those in relation to matters listed in the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution. The State legislatures are to consider the 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule for devolution of power and responsibilities to Panchayats. Accordingly, all matters relating to Panchayats, including, implementing local development works, manpower requirement, financial resources, administrative powers at the Panchayat level and enhancement of the financial and administrative autonomy of Panchayats, etc. fall within the purview of State Government. During the 15 th Finance Commission (FC) award period (FY 2020-21 to FY 2025-26), including the interim period of FY 2020-21, a total of Rs. 2,82,632 Crores have been released against the total allocation of Rs. 2,97,555 Crores. The State-wise details of allocation & release of the funds under 15 th FC is placed at Annexure I . Further, under the Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) of the Ministry, a total of Rs. 3601.77 Crores have been released to the States/UT during the last five year from FY 2021-22. The details of funds released to the States/UTs under the Revamped RGSA scheme during the last five years is at Annexure-II . As part of the Digital India initiative, MoPR has established an integrated digital governance ecosystem for Panchayats to promote transparency, accountability, and efficient financial management. This Ministry has launched ‘eGramSwaraj’ in 2020–21 as a unified digital platform which supports end-to-end planning, budgeting, accounting, monitoring, and online payments. Its integration with the Public Financial Management System (PFMS), Government e-Marketplace (GeM), and AuditOnline has enabled seamless fund flow, transparent procurement, payments and auditing, thereby strengthening governance and financial oversight at the grassroots. title: 38th Webinar of the National Good Governance Webinar Series 2026-27 under the theme ‘Sustainability and Replication of the Awarded Initiatives under PMA’ held on 28th July 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions 38th Webinar of the National Good Governance Webinar Series 2026-27 under the theme ‘Sustainability and Replication of the Awarded Initiatives under PMA’ held on 28th July 2026 Presentations made on Solar-Powered Water Schemes under the National Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) initiative and its Sustainability, by Shri Anurag Srivastava, and its expansion & implementation in Minor Irrigation Department by Shri Devendra Kumar to national audience प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi Hon’ble Prime Minister had directed Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), in April 2022, to hold virtual conferences/ webinars with District Collectors and other officers in which past award winners of PM’s Awards (PMA) for Excellence in Public Administration be invited to present their experiences with the objective of greater dissemination and replication. Since then, 37 webinars have been held so far. Each webinar is attended by about 1000 officials from Line Departments, State Governments, District Collectors, State Administrative Training Institutes and Central Training Institutes. The 38 th National Good Governance Webinar was held on the 28 th July 2026 in which the initiative of Solar-Powered Water Schemes under the National Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) awarded with the PM’s Award for Excellence in Public Administration, 2023 was presented under the theme ‘ Sustainability and Replication of the Initiatives Awarded under PMA ’. The Presentations included: The awarded initiative and  Sustainability aspects of the initiative  presented by Shri Anurag Srivastava, Addl. Chief Secretary, Namami Gange & Rural Water Supply Department, Govt. of Uttar Pradesh; and Implementation of the key aspects & further scaling up in Minor Irrigation Department by Shri Devendra Kumar, Chief Engineer, Minor Irrigation Department. The Webinar was chaired by Shri Puneet Yadav, Additional Secretary, DARPG and was attended by senior officers of the Department. The Webinar was attended from more than 2200 locations across India with Senior Officials of Administrative Reforms Departments of States/UTs, District Collectors, State and District field officers, Officers of Central and State Administrative Training Institutes. ***** Anand (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290722) आगंतुक पटल  : 62 Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions 38th Webinar of the National Good Governance Webinar Series 2026-27 under the theme ‘Sustainability and Replication of the Awarded Initiatives under PMA’ held on 28th July 2026 Presentations made on Solar-Powered Water Schemes under the National Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) initiative and its Sustainability, by Shri Anurag Srivastava, and its expansion & implementation in Minor Irrigation Department by Shri Devendra Kumar to national audience प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Says Public Examinations Amendment Bill Will Further Strengthen Legal Framework Against Examination Malpractices
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions Dr. Jitendra Singh Says Public Examinations Amendment Bill Will Further Strengthen Legal Framework Against Examination Malpractices Government committed to safeguarding the future of students and ensuring integrity, transparency and credibility of public examinations Amendment Bill Aims to Reward Merit and Strengthen Credibility of Public Examinations: Dr. Jitendra Singh प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today said that the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 is a significant step towards further strengthening the legal framework to curb examination-related malpractices and protect the interests of students and youth across the country. Initiating the discussion on the Bill in the Lok Sabha, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the legislation reaffirms the Government's commitment to safeguarding the future of students and reflects Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's resolve to ensure that no one is allowed to compromise with the aspirations of the country's youth. He described the legislation as a milestone in strengthening the integrity of India's public examination system. The Minister said incidents of question paper leakages and examination-related malpractices have occurred across different States over the years, highlighting the need for a comprehensive national legal framework. He noted that the Government enacted the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 as the country's first comprehensive legislation to deal with unfair means in public examinations and is now proposing further amendments based on the experience gained during its implementation to make the law more stringent and effective. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Act covers examinations conducted by major recruitment agencies, including the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS), as well as the National Testing Agency (NTA) for higher education admissions. He recalled that the 2024 Act made offences under its ambit cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable with stringent penal provisions. Highlighting the key provisions of the Amendment Bill, the Minister said the punishment for persons resorting to unfair means is proposed to be enhanced from imprisonment of three to five years to five to ten years, while the maximum fine is proposed to be increased from ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh. For service providers involved in such offences, the maximum fine is proposed to be increased from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore and the period of debarment from conducting public examinations from four years to eight years. Punishment for directors and senior management of service providers is also proposed to be enhanced from three to ten years' imprisonment to five to ten years, with the maximum fine being increased from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore. The Bill further proposes to increase the punishment for organised crime from five to ten years' imprisonment to seven to ten years and enhance the maximum fine from ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore. Emphasising the importance of speedy justice, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Amendment Bill provides for the establishment of Special Fast Track Courts to deal with offences relating to public examinations. He said the Bill envisages completion of investigation within two months and completion of trial within three months from the date of filing of the charge sheet, ensuring expeditious disposal of such cases. The Bill also empowers the Central Government to refer investigation of offences under the Act to a Special Task Force constituted for the purpose, thereby enabling swift and effective action against organised examination-related crimes. The Minister informed the House that the Government has already initiated steps for establishment of Special Fast Track Courts in several locations to facilitate speedy disposal of such cases. He also referred to the Prime Minister's announcement of a high-level task force comprising eminent experts to make the public examination system "leak-proof". He added that substantial progress has already been made in implementing the recommendations of the committee constituted to strengthen the examination ecosystem. He said the objective of the amendments is to ensure that students are rewarded for their genuine efforts while enhancing the credibility, transparency and fairness of public examinations. Concluding his remarks, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the proposed amendments would reinforce deterrence against organised examination-related crimes, ensure speedy justice and further strengthen public confidence in the integrity, transparency and fairness of the country's public examination system. ***** NKR/AV (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290606) आगंतुक पटल  : 148 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Marathi , Gujarati Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions Dr. Jitendra Singh Says Public Examinations Amendment Bill Will Further Strengthen Legal Framework Against Examination Malpractices Government committed to safeguarding the future of students and ensuring integrity, transparency and credibility of public examinations Amendment Bill Aims to Reward Merit and Strengthen Credibility of Public Examinations: Dr. Jitendra Singh प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: India's First Direct Commercial Container Freight Train Reaches Nepal, Opening a New Chapter in Cross-border Trade and Connectivity
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Railways India's First Direct Commercial Container Freight Train Reaches Nepal, Opening a New Chapter in Cross-border Trade and Connectivity 40-Wagon Freight Train from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar Operates Under Revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol Direct Rail Freight Service Reduces Transit Time, Logistics Costs and Cargo Handling, Strengthening India-Nepal Trade Ties प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:16PM by PIB Delhi Indian Railways has achieved a major milestone in strengthening India-Nepal freight connectivity with the successful operation of the first-ever direct commercial container freight train from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar Customs Yard, Nepal. The train, comprising 40 wagons carrying a consignment of canola, completed its journey under the revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol, marking a new chapter in rail-based cross-border freight movement. The successful operation enables direct rail movement of containerised cargo from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar without transshipment at the border. The new arrangement is expected to substantially reduce transit time, logistics costs and cargo handling while improving the efficiency, reliability and competitiveness of cross-border trade between the two neighbouring countries. The milestone has been made possible through the implementation of the revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol, which facilitates seamless end-to-end rail transportation of freight between the two countries. The achievement builds upon the broad-gauge rail link between Jogbani (India) and Biratnagar (Nepal), inaugurated in June 2023 by the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India Shri Narendra Modi and the then Prime Minister of Nepal. Following the signing of the revised Letter of Exchange (LoE) in November 2025, direct commercial rail movement to Biratnagar has now become operational, opening new opportunities for bilateral trade and economic cooperation. The direct freight service is expected to provide a significant boost to the movement of import and export cargo by offering a faster, more economical and environmentally sustainable mode of transportation. By reducing multiple handling points and improving supply chain efficiency, the initiative will benefit exporters, importers, logistics operators and industries engaged in cross-border trade. The milestone also reflects Indian Railways' continued focus on expanding international rail connectivity, strengthening freight logistics and supporting the Government's vision of improving ease of doing business through modern transport infrastructure. Increased rail-based freight movement will contribute to lower logistics costs, improved cargo reliability and greener transportation while fostering stronger economic partnerships with neighbouring countries. The successful operation of the first direct commercial container freight train to Nepal marks another important achievement in Indian Railways' efforts to build an integrated, efficient and future-ready freight network that supports regional trade, economic growth and seamless international connectivity. ***** Mahesh Kumar / Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290444) आगंतुक पटल  : 415 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Gujarati , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of Railways India's First Direct Commercial Container Freight Train Reaches Nepal, Opening a New Chapter in Cross-border Trade and Connectivity 40-Wagon Freight Train from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar Operates Under Revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol Direct Rail Freight Service Reduces Transit Time, Logistics Costs and Cargo Handling, Strengthening India-Nepal Trade Ties प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Indian Railways Approves ₹163 Crore Electric Traction Upgradation for Parbhani-Mudkhed Section in Nanded Division of South Central Railway
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Approves ₹163 Crore Electric Traction Upgradation for Parbhani-Mudkhed Section in Nanded Division of South Central Railway Traction System Upgrade Over 164 Track Km to Handle Higher Freight Volumes and Support Running of Vande Bharat Express Trains प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 1:39PM by PIB Delhi In a significant step towards strengthening railway infrastructure and enhancing network capacity, Indian Railways has sanctioned the upgradation of the electric traction system on the Parbhani-Mudkhed double line section in Nanded Division of South Central Railway. The project, which also includes associated power supply installation works, has been sanctioned at a cost of Rs. 163 crore. The project involves converting the existing 1x25 kV electric traction system to a more advanced 2x25 kV system over a stretch of 164 Track Kilometres, supported by upgraded power supply infrastructure to meet the enhanced electrical load. The Parbhani-Mudkhed section forms part of the strategically important Highly Utilised Network (HUN) Route-9, connecting Ajmer-Indore-Khandwa-Akola-Purna-Mudkhed-Secunderabad-Mahbubnagar-Dhone. The upgraded traction system will strengthen power supply for train operations, enabling the section to handle higher freight volumes and support the running of Vande Bharat Express trains. It will also contribute to Indian Railways' goal of achieving 3,000 Million Tonnes of freight loading by 2029-30. The project reflects Indian Railways' continuing efforts to modernise electrical infrastructure and improve operational efficiency on high-density corridors across the country. ***** Mahesh Kumar / Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290300) आगंतुक पटल  : 411 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu , Kannada Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Approves ₹163 Crore Electric Traction Upgradation for Parbhani-Mudkhed Section in Nanded Division of South Central Railway Traction System Upgrade Over 164 Track Km to Handle Higher Freight Volumes and Support Running of Vande Bharat Express Trains प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: NHAI Undertakes DPR Preparation to Decongest Sarai Kale Khan Loop on DND–Sohna National Highway Corridor
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Road Transport & Highways NHAI Undertakes DPR Preparation to Decongest Sarai Kale Khan Loop on DND–Sohna National Highway Corridor प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi In order to improve traffic flow and enhance commuter convenience in the National Capital Region (NCR), NHAI has undertaken preparation of the Detailed Project Report (DPR) to address traffic congestion at the Sarai Kale Khan Loop, which is a critical junction of the DND–Sohna section on NH-148NA. The DPR will examine long-term traffic management and engineering solutions for one of the busiest transport nodes in Delhi and will complement the ongoing infrastructure development initiatives in the region. The Sarai Kale Khan Loop serves as a strategic convergence point for traffic originating from Ashram, Noida and Sarai Kale Khan. With the upcoming commissioning of the DND–Sohna National Highway corridor, the location is expected to witness a substantial increase in traffic volumes, necessitating timely intervention to ensure smooth and efficient traffic movement. Recognizing the strategic importance of the corridor, NHAI will undertake DPR preparation on priority to identify comprehensive engineering solutions to decongest the junction and improve traffic circulation. The DPR will evaluate suitable infrastructure interventions aimed at enhancing capacity, reducing travel time and ensuring safety as well as more efficient movement of vehicles through the corridor. It will also ensure that the operational benefits of the DND–Sohna corridor are fully realized upon its commissioning by enabling seamless connectivity at this critical interchange. The initiative reflects NHAI's continued focus on improving urban connectivity, reducing congestion and delivering enhanced travel experience for road users. *** GDH/DS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290462) आगंतुक पटल  : 180 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Road Transport & Highways NHAI Undertakes DPR Preparation to Decongest Sarai Kale Khan Loop on DND–Sohna National Highway Corridor प्रविष्टि तिथि:

The Sarai Kale Khan Loop serves as a strategic convergence point for traffic originating from Ashram, Noida and Sarai Kale Khan. With the upcoming commissioning of the DND–Sohna National Highway corridor, the location is expected to witness a substantial increase in traffic volumes, necessitating timely intervention to ensure smooth and efficient traffic movement. Recognizing the strategic importance of the corridor, NHAI will undertake DPR preparation on priority to identify comprehensive engineering solutions to decongest the junction and improve traffic circulation. The DPR will evaluate suitable infrastructure interventions aimed at enhancing capacity, reducing travel time and ensuring safety as well as more efficient movement of vehicles through the corridor. It will also ensure that the operational benefits of the DND–Sohna corridor are fully realized upon its commissioning by enabling seamless connectivity at this critical interchange. The initiative reflects NHAI's continued focus on improving urban connectivity, reducing congestion and delivering enhanced travel experience for road users. *** GDH/DS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290462)

Under NFBS, financial assistance is released to the States/UTs based on proposals received from them, subject to the State/UT-wise beneficiary cap. States/UTs are regularly requested through letters, review meetings to submit complete proposals in a timely manner to facilitate early processing and disbursement of benefits. title: BENEFICIARIES UNDER RSETIS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development BENEFICIARIES UNDER RSETIS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:33PM by PIB Delhi The district-wise details of beneficiaries trained under the Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs), the number of candidates who completed training, other details of training programmes conducted like number of training programmes conducted District wise, and the number of candidates settled/self-employed during the last five years are provided at https://kaushal.rural.gov.in/assets/files/PQ_1530_English.pdf . RSETIs conduct demand- driven Skill Development Programmes (SDPs), Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDPs) and Entrepreneurship Awareness Programmes (EAPs) to promote self-employment among rural unemployed youth. To strengthen the functioning of RSETIs, particularly in districts with comparatively low beneficiary coverage or settlement rates, the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) undertakes regular monitoring through the Management Information System (MIS portal), conducts review meetings, promotes convergence with State Rural Livelihood Missions (SRLMs) and other stakeholders for beneficiary mobilization, facilitates post-training handholding and bank credit linkage, and provides capacity building and guidance to improve training quality and settlement outcomes RSETI is a demand-driven Scheme under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), and funds are released to the States/UTs on a reimbursement basis. The State-wise details of funds released under the programme during the last five years and district-wise details for Andhra Pradesh, are given in Annexure-I (A&B) . The State and district-wise details of women, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward classes and vulnerable groups trained and settled under RSETI during the last five years including Andhra Pradesh are given at https://kaushal.rural.gov.in/assets/files/PQ_1530_English.pdf. MoRD promotes targeted mobilisation of eligible rural youth, particularly women, SCs, STs and other vulnerable groups, through convergence with State Rural Livelihood Missions (SRLMs), District Rural Development Agencies (DRDAs), Self Help Groups (SHGs) and other stakeholders. RSETIs conduct need-based, women-centric and SC/ST-focused skill and entrepreneurship development programmes. Post-training support includes counselling, mentoring, facilitation of bank credit linkage, enterprise establishment support and regular follow-up to promote sustainable self-employment and improved settlement outcomes. title: SHGS MAPPED ON DIGITAL PLATFORMS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development SHGS MAPPED ON DIGITAL PLATFORMS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi A total of 10.05 crore rural households and 92 lakh women Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are mapped on the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) digital platform. The Ministry maintains data on financial linkage and credit access of women Self Help Groups (SHGs) under DAY-NRLM through the SHG Bank Linkage Portal, which captures information on the credit accessed by SHGs from banks. The total credit disbursement to the SHGs is Rs. 13,41,852.66 crores. A dedicated mobile application has been developed to capture and manage the profiles of entrepreneurs and their enterprises. Training on the operation and use of the application is conducted for the concerned stakeholders, and data entry is carried out through the application. It supports planning, monitoring and strengthening rural livelihoods under DAY-NRLM. This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development DR. title: ACTION PLAN UNDER LAKHPATI DIDI INITIATIVE
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development ACTION PLAN UNDER LAKHPATI DIDI INITIATIVE प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi Lakhpati Didi initiative is an outcome of Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme being implemented by Ministry in partnership of States and UTs (except Chandigarh and Delhi), with the objective to improve the livelihoods of poor rural households in country, and organise rural households into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) for their social and financial inclusion. Lakhpati Didi initiative is to empower and enable Self-Help Groups (SHG) Women, earn a minimum income of Rupees one lakh per annum on a sustainable basis, for at least 4 agricultural seasons and/ or business cycles. Under the DAY-NRLM, 10.08 crore rural households have been mobilised into around 92 lakh Self Help Groups (SHGs) across the country. As on date, more than 3.46 crore SHG members have been enabled as Lakhpati Didis. In Madhya Pradesh, 23,67,520 SHG members have been enabled as Lakhpati Didis, including around 46,000 SHG members in Chhindwara district. DAY-NRLM is providing entrepreneurship support in the country including Madhya Pradesh, through Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP), a sub-scheme under the DAY-NRLM program that supports and facilitates the SHGs and their family members to set-up small enterprises in the non-farm sector, create an eco-system of entrepreneurship in a block by providing trainings and hand-holding support through the Community Resource Person for Enterprise promotion (CRP-EP), finance through Community Enterprise Fund (CEF), domain and business related mentorship. As of June 2026, 4.32 lakh enterprises have been supported under SVEP in country including 30,573 in Madhya Pradesh. DAY-NRLM is also providing access to credit and microfinance facilities to empower women through various steps which are as follows: Funds are provided to SHGs in the form of Revolving Fund (RF) and Community Investment Fund (CIF) to help them in creating a corpus, from which the SHG members can avail loans for various purposes. The SHGs are also facilitated for Bank linkage for accessing credit at subsidized rates of interest. Since 2013-14, the SHGs have been assisted to access Bank credit of Rs. 13.41 lakh crores, so far. SHG members are also imparted financial literacy skills through trainings on accounting, record-keeping, budgeting, and loan management etc. DAY-NRLM also facilitates universal access to cost-effective and reliable financial services to the poor and it works on both demand and supply sides of financial inclusion by promoting financial literacy among the poor and providing catalytic capital to the SHGs and their federations. The promotion of digital finance is done through deployment of SHG Women as Banking Correspondent Sakhi (BC Sakhi), with the support of banks and Common Service Centers. Under DAY-NRLM, regular trainings and capacity-building programmes are conducted for SHG members and community cadres on SHG management, financial literacy, livelihood promotion and enterprise development to ensure effective implementation of DAY-NRLM across all States. DAY-NRLM also strengthens market access for SHG products in all States/UTs including Madhya Pradesh through a comprehensive branding and marketing ecosystem. The Ministry has registered the brands “Saras”, “Saras Aajeevika” and “Aajeevika” for promoting SHG products, while 25 States have developed their own State-level brands, such as UMED (Maharashtra), Palash and Adiva (Jharkhand), Himira (Himachal Pradesh) and Mathi (Tamil Nadu). To further enhance market access, Saras Melas are organised at the National, Regional, State and District levels, including two National-level Saras Melas, one Saras Food Festival and more than 50 State-level Saras Melas every year. The Ministry also operates the Saras Aajeevika Gallery in Central Delhi for the sale of curated SHG products, while several States have established permanent retail outlets under their respective State brands. In addition, the Ministry has developed the eSaras e-commerce platform and partnered with GeM, ONDC, Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho and JioMart to expand market reach and sales opportunities for SHG products. This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development DR. title: ALLOCATION OF BUDGET UNDER DDU-GKY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development ALLOCATION OF BUDGET UNDER DDU-GKY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:29PM by PIB Delhi Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is one of the cluster of initiatives under Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through placement-linked skilling programs. The cumulative details of funds sanctioned/released and expenditure incurred under DDU-GKY during the last five years and the current year are given in Annexure-I . Under DDUGKY, a total of 18.45 lakh candidates have been trained, 11.44 lakh candidates have been certified and 12.35 lakh have been placed since inception i.e. 2014-15. The quality of training and employability are ensured by the scheme design wherein Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) are reimbursed allowable funds only after ensuring 6 months of employment for at least 70% of the trained and certified beneficiaries. Further, an impact assessment study has been conducted through Transrural Agri Consulting Services Pvt. Ltd. in the year 2025. The income enhancement indicator as per the evaluation study has shown that beneficiaries experienced an average salary growth of 30.79% in a period of three years with an average salary of ₹ 16,500 per month. DDU-GKY incorporates mandatory social inclusion norms to ensure equitable access to training and placement opportunities for disadvantaged groups. The Scheme mandates that 50% of candidates shall be from SC/ST communities, 33% shall be women, and 3% shall be Persons with Disabilities (PwDs). In order to ensure strengthening skill development, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihood opportunities for rural youth under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY), a number of steps have been taken. These include: Shifting to Batch-Mode payments in place of the earlier project-mode system, enabling faster and more accountable disbursals. Greater emphasis has been placed on securing a minimum of 6 months of employment for trained candidates, along with tracking support for 12 months to ensure job continuity. Earlier a minimum of 3 month of employment was mandated. The scope of the programme has been expanded to include self-employment and emerging gig economy opportunities, promoting entrepreneurial capabilities among the rural youth and encouraging local enterprise development. title: VIKSIT GRAM PANCHAYAT PLAN
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development VIKSIT GRAM PANCHAYAT PLAN प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 6:27PM by PIB Delhi Under Section 16 of the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025 , every Gram Panchayat is required to prepare a Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan (VGPP) through a participatory planning process. The Gram Sabha identifies and prioritises the permissible works required for the holistic development of the Gram Panchayat, and the Gram Panchayat prepares the VGPP in accordance with the provisions of the Act. The approved VGPP is thereafter consolidated at the Intermediate and District Panchayat levels for preparation of the aggregate Block and District Plans under the Mission. Yuktdhara is a GIS-based planning support tool that assists authorised functionaries in scientific planning by providing geospatial information and analytical inputs for the identification, prioritisation and planning of permissible works, thereby supporting the preparation of the VGPP. Access to the Yuktdhara portal is provided to authorised functionaries designated by the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations in accordance with the prescribed operational framework. As per Section 21 of the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025 , the State Government is responsible for providing the necessary staff and technical support, including Rozgar Sahayaks and Computer Operators , to the District Programme Coordinator and the Programme Officer for the effective implementation of the Programme. These matters such as the manner by which the rozgar sahayaks and computer operators work fall within the administrative domain of the respective States/Union Territories. The Ministry accords high priority to capacity building of all stakeholders for effective implementation of VB–G RAM G. Training programmes are being organised at the National, State, District, Block and Gram Panchayat levels through a cascading training framework covering the preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs), technology-enabled planning and monitoring tools including use of Yuktdhara. Detailed training modules, user manuals, standard operating procedures and digital learning resources like e-Saksham have also been made available with the States/Union Territories to facilitate effective implementation and strengthen participatory planning through Gram Sabhas. Also, Capacity Building is an ongoing process and as per the needs and requirements of the States/UTs the technical tram send by the Ministry to the respective States/UTs. Under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G, Mates engaged under the Scheme are paid wages at the semi-skilled wage rate, as notified by the respective State Government/Union Territory Administration in accordance with the applicable wage notifications. The wage rates payable to Mates are determined by the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations.
